Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Hydroxyi
-/
import TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.SavitchARM.Run
import TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.SavitchARM.Reach

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# The midpoint recursion of the Savitch register machine

The recursive part of `Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.A` computes midpoint reachability:
started at label `cl` on a node `(U, V)` at level `I = i`, with any stack contents of the
right size below it, the machine returns at label `rt b` with `b` the truth value of
`Reach (2 ^ w) R i U V` — with the same registers, except the scratch midpoint register `M`
(`Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.call_spec`). Here `R` is the step relation answered by
decider `3` on codes at radius `s`.

The proof is an induction on the level, mirroring the recursion of [AB09, §4.2.1, proof of
Theorem 4.14]: at a positive level the midpoint loop (`loop_spec`) descends into the first
half (`desc1`, pushing `(V, 0)`), and, if that half is reachable, into the second half
(`desc2`, pushing `(U, 1)`); every return pops the frame it pushed (`pop_run`) and dispatches
on its phase bit. The stack invariant `Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Inv` bounds the
`w`-bit-digit stack `SE` by `2 ^ (w (w - i))` and the phase stack `SP` by `2 ^ (w - i)`, so
every register stays below `2 ^ (w · w)`.

## Main definitions

* `Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Rel` — the step relation read from the oracle, with its
  defining equation `rel_iff_orc`.
* `Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Inv` — the register invariant at a level.

## Main results

* `Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.call_spec` — the recursion computes `Reach`.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§4.2.1, Theorem 4.14.)
-/

namespace Complexity.LogProg

namespace SavitchARM

open Turing

/-- **The step relation read from the oracle**: decider `3` accepts
`⟨x, ⟨bits u, ⟨bits v, bits s⟩⟩⟩`. -/
def Rel (orc : Fin 4 → List Bool → Bool) (x : List Bool) (s u v : ℕ) : Prop :=
  orc 3 (pairEncode x (pairEncode (Nat.bits u) (pairEncode (Nat.bits v) (Nat.bits s)))) = true

/-- `Rel orc x s u v` holds exactly when decider `3` accepts `⟨x, ⟨bits u, ⟨bits v, bits s⟩⟩⟩`:
`orc 3 (pairEncode x (pairEncode (bits u) (pairEncode (bits v) (bits s)))) = true`. -/
theorem rel_iff_orc {orc : Fin 4 → List Bool → Bool} {x : List Bool} {s u v : ℕ} :
    Rel orc x s u v ↔
      orc 3 (pairEncode x (pairEncode (Nat.bits u) (pairEncode (Nat.bits v) (Nat.bits s)))) =
        true :=
  Iff.rfl

/-- **The register invariant at level `i`**: the setup registers and the scratch registers
are clear, the radius, width and code bound are in place, the node's codes are below
`2 ^ w`, the midpoint is at most `2 ^ w`, and the two stacks hold at most `w - i` frames. -/
structure Inv (s w i : ℕ) (st : St) : Prop where
  /-- the input-length counter is clear -/
  hn : st.n = 0
  /-- the base register is clear -/
  ha : st.a = 0
  /-- the exponent counter is clear -/
  hX : st.X = 0
  /-- the power accumulator is clear -/
  hP : st.P = 0
  /-- the scratch register `T` is clear -/
  hT : st.T = 0
  /-- the scratch register `Z` is clear -/
  hZ : st.Z = 0
  /-- the loop counter is clear -/
  hC : st.C = 0
  /-- the scratch register `Q` is clear -/
  hQ : st.Q = 0
  /-- the popped-endpoint register is clear -/
  hE : st.E = 0
  /-- the radius is `s` -/
  hs : st.s = s
  /-- the width is `w` -/
  hw : st.w = w
  /-- the code bound is `2 ^ w` -/
  hK : st.K = 2 ^ w
  /-- the source code is below `2 ^ w` -/
  hU : st.U < 2 ^ w
  /-- the target code is below `2 ^ w` -/
  hV : st.V < 2 ^ w
  /-- the midpoint is at most `2 ^ w` -/
  hM : st.M ≤ 2 ^ w
  /-- the level is `i` -/
  hI : st.I = i
  /-- the endpoint stack holds at most `w - i` digits of `w` bits -/
  hSE : st.SE < 2 ^ (w * (w - i))
  /-- the phase stack holds at most `w - i` bits -/
  hSP : st.SP < 2 ^ (w - i)

/-- The basic size facts: `w ≤ 2 ^ w ≤ 2 ^ (w · w)`. -/
lemma size_facts (w : ℕ) : w < 2 ^ w ∧ 2 ^ w ≤ 2 ^ (w * w) :=
  ⟨Nat.lt_two_pow_self, Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) (Nat.le_mul_self w)⟩

/-- **The invariant bounds the registers** by `2 ^ (w · w)`. -/
lemma Inv.bd {s w i : ℕ} {st : St} (h : Inv s w i st) (hsw : s ≤ w) (hi : i ≤ w) :
    st.Bd (2 ^ (w * w)) := by
  obtain ⟨f1, f2⟩ := size_facts w
  have g1 : 2 ^ (w * (w - i)) ≤ 2 ^ (w * w) :=
    Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) (Nat.mul_le_mul_left _ (by omega))
  have g2 : 2 ^ (w - i) ≤ 2 ^ w := Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) (by omega)
  have := h.hn; have := h.ha; have := h.hX; have := h.hP; have := h.hT; have := h.hZ
  have := h.hC; have := h.hQ; have := h.hE; have := h.hs; have := h.hw; have := h.hK
  have := h.hU; have := h.hV; have := h.hM; have := h.hI; have := h.hSE; have := h.hSP
  simp only [St.Bd]
  omega

/-- **Pushing a digit keeps the stack within one more frame**: `SE < 2 ^ (w (w - (i + 1)))`
and `v < 2 ^ w` give `SE · 2 ^ w + v < 2 ^ (w (w - i))`. -/
lemma push_lt {w i SE v : ℕ} (hi : i + 1 ≤ w) (hSE : SE < 2 ^ (w * (w - (i + 1))))
    (hv : v < 2 ^ w) : SE * 2 ^ w + v < 2 ^ (w * (w - i)) := by
  have e : w * (w - i) = w * (w - (i + 1)) + w := by
    rw [show w - i = w - (i + 1) + 1 by omega, Nat.mul_succ]
  rw [e, pow_add]
  have : (SE + 1) * 2 ^ w ≤ 2 ^ (w * (w - (i + 1))) * 2 ^ w :=
    Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ hSE
  rw [Nat.add_mul, one_mul] at this
  omega

/-- Pushing a phase bit keeps the phase stack within one more frame. -/
lemma pushP_lt {w i SP : ℕ} (hi : i + 1 ≤ w) (hSP : SP < 2 ^ (w - (i + 1))) :
    2 * SP + 1 < 2 ^ (w - i) := by
  rw [show w - i = w - (i + 1) + 1 by omega, pow_succ]
  omega

variable {E : ℕ} {orc : Fin 4 → List Bool → Bool} {x : List Bool} {s w : ℕ}

open Classical in
/-- **The base case**: at level `0` the machine answers `U = V ∨ R U V`.

**Proof sketch.** `cl` sees `I = 0` and calls decider `3` on `⟨x, ⟨bits U, ⟨bits V, bits s⟩⟩⟩`;
on a negative answer it compares `U` with `V`. -/
theorem base_spec (hsw : s ≤ w) (st : St) (h : Inv s w 0 st) :
    AReach (A E) orc x (GuardLe (A E) x (2 ^ (w * w))) (some .cl, st.toV, none)
      (some (.rt (decide (Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) 0 st.U st.V))), st.toV, none) := by
  have hbd := h.bd hsw (Nat.zero_le _)
  refine step_of hbd ?_
  regs [astep, A, h.hI, ↓reduceIte]
  refine step_of hbd ?_
  simp only [astep, A, vword_whole₃]
  regs [h.hs]
  by_cases hr : Rel orc x s st.U st.V
  · have hr' : orc 3 (pairEncode x (pairEncode (Nat.bits st.U)
        (pairEncode (Nat.bits st.V) (Nat.bits s)))) = true := hr
    rw [if_pos hr', decide_eq_true (show Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) 0 st.U st.V from Or.inr hr)]
    exact AReach.refl _
  · have hr' : ¬ orc 3 (pairEncode x (pairEncode (Nat.bits st.U)
        (pairEncode (Nat.bits st.V) (Nat.bits s)))) = true := hr
    rw [if_neg hr']
    refine step_of hbd ?_
    regs [astep, A]
    by_cases he : st.U = st.V
    · rw [if_pos he, decide_eq_true (show Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) 0 st.U st.V from Or.inl he)]
      exact AReach.refl _
    · rw [if_neg he, decide_eq_false (show ¬ Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) 0 st.U st.V by
        rintro (h1 | h1) <;> contradiction)]
      exact AReach.refl _

/-- Close a register-file bound from the unfolded bounds in context. -/
scoped macro "bdt" : tactic => `(tactic| (simp only [St.Bd]; omega))

variable (E orc x s w) in
open Classical in
/-- **The recursion is correct at level `i`**: from `cl` on any register file meeting the
invariant at level `i`, the machine reaches `rt b`, `b` the truth value of
`Reach (2 ^ w) R i U V`, changing only the midpoint register (to a value at most `2 ^ w`). -/
def CallOK (i : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ st, Inv s w i st → ∃ M', M' ≤ 2 ^ w ∧
    AReach (A E) orc x (GuardLe (A E) x (2 ^ (w * w))) (some .cl, st.toV, none)
      (some (.rt (decide (Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) i st.U st.V))),
        St.toV { st with M := M' }, none)

open Classical in
/-- **The first descent**: from `loop` at level `i + 1` with midpoint `m = M < 2 ^ w`, the
machine pushes `(V, 0)`, evaluates the first half `(U, m)` at level `i`, pops the frame, and
reaches `cp (push true)` if the first half is reachable and `a0F` otherwise, with `V = m`
and the popped endpoint in `E`.

**Proof sketch.** `pushV_run`, the move of `M` into `V` and the decrement of `I`; the
recursion at level `i` (`CallOK`); at `rt b` the level is below `w`, so `pop_run` restores
`SE` and returns the saved `V` in `E`; `I` is incremented, the even phase stack selects
`h0`, which halves it back. -/
theorem desc1 (hsw : s ≤ w) (i : ℕ) (hi : i + 1 ≤ w) (IH : CallOK E orc x s w i) (st : St)
    (h : Inv s w (i + 1) st) (hm : st.M < 2 ^ w) :
    ∃ M1, M1 ≤ 2 ^ w ∧ AReach (A E) orc x (GuardLe (A E) x (2 ^ (w * w))) (some .loop, st.toV, none)
      (some (if decide (Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) i st.U st.M) then .cp (.push true) 0
        else .a0F), St.toV { st with V := st.M, M := M1, E := st.V }, none) := by
  obtain ⟨f1, f2⟩ := size_facts w
  have hbd := h.bd hsw hi
  have hSE1 := push_lt hi h.hSE h.hV
  have hSP1 := pushP_lt hi h.hSP
  have g1 : 2 ^ (w * (w - i)) ≤ 2 ^ (w * w) :=
    Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) (Nat.mul_le_mul_left _ (by omega))
  have g2 : 2 ^ (w - i) ≤ 2 ^ w := Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) (by omega)
  have h3 : Inv s w i
      { st with SE := st.SE * 2 ^ w + st.V, V := st.M, SP := 2 * st.SP, M := 0, I := i } :=
    ⟨h.hn, h.ha, h.hX, h.hP, h.hT, h.hZ, h.hC, h.hQ, h.hE, h.hs, h.hw, h.hK, h.hU, hm,
      Nat.zero_le _, rfl, hSE1, by show 2 * st.SP < 2 ^ (w - i); omega⟩
  obtain ⟨M1, hM1, hc⟩ := IH _ h3
  dsimp only at hc
  refine ⟨M1, hM1, ?_⟩
  have hw := h.hw
  -- `loop`: the midpoint is below `K`
  refine step_of hbd ?_
  regs [astep, A, if_neg (show st.M ≠ st.K by rw [h.hK]; exact hm.ne)]
  -- push `(V, 0)`
  refine (pushV_run st h.hC h.hT h.hZ hbd (by rw [hw]; omega) (by omega)).trans ?_
  have hbd1 : St.Bd (2 ^ (w * w))
      { st with SE := st.SE * 2 ^ st.w + st.V, V := 0, SP := 2 * st.SP } := by
    have := hbd; simp only [St.Bd] at this ⊢; rw [hw]; omega
  have hMB : st.M ≤ 2 ^ (w * w) := by omega
  refine (mv_run .descM _ hbd1 (by regs [mvDst, mvSrc]; omega)).trans ?_
  regs [mvDst, mvSrc, mvExit, zero_add]
  have hbd2 : St.Bd (2 ^ (w * w))
      { st with SE := st.SE * 2 ^ st.w + st.V, V := st.M, SP := 2 * st.SP, M := 0 } := by
    have := hbd; simp only [St.Bd] at this ⊢; rw [hw]; omega
  refine step_of hbd2 ?_
  regs [astep, A]
  refine cont (by ext <;> simp [hw, h.hI]) (hc.trans ?_)
  -- `rt b`: not the root, pop the frame
  have hbd4 := (h3.bd hsw (by omega))
  have hbd4' : St.Bd (2 ^ (w * w))
      { st with SE := st.SE * 2 ^ w + st.V, V := st.M, SP := 2 * st.SP, M := M1, I := i } := by
    simp only [St.Bd] at hbd4 ⊢; omega
  refine step_of hbd4' ?_
  regs [astep, A, if_neg (show i ≠ st.w by omega)]
  refine (pop_run _
    { st with SE := st.SE * 2 ^ w + st.V, V := st.M, SP := 2 * st.SP, M := M1, I := i }
    st.SE st.V h.hC h.hT h.hZ h.hQ h.hE hbd4' (by simp [hw]) (by simp [hw]; exact h.hV)).trans ?_
  have hbd5 : St.Bd (2 ^ (w * w))
      { st with SE := st.SE, V := st.M, SP := 2 * st.SP, M := M1, I := i, E := st.V } := by
    have := Nat.le_mul_of_pos_right st.SE (Nat.two_pow_pos w)
    simp only [St.Bd] at hbd4 ⊢; have := h.hV; omega
  refine step_of hbd5 ?_
  regs [astep, A]
  have hbd6 : St.Bd (2 ^ (w * w))
      { st with SE := st.SE, V := st.M, SP := 2 * st.SP, M := M1, I := i + 1, E := st.V } := by
    simp only [St.Bd] at hbd5 ⊢; omega
  refine step_of hbd6 ?_
  regs [astep, A, Nat.mul_mod_right, zero_ne_one, if_false]
  refine step_of hbd6 ?_
  regs [astep, A]
  refine reach_of_eq (AReach.refl _) ?_
  congr 3
  ext <;> simp [h.hI]

open Classical in
/-- **The second descent**: from `cp (push true)` after a reachable first half (`V = m`,
`E` the saved target), the machine pushes `(U, 1)`, evaluates the second half `(m, V)` at
level `i`, pops the frame, and reaches `a1T` if the second half is reachable and `a1F`
otherwise, with `U = m` and the saved source in `E`.

**Proof sketch.** `pushU_run`, the increment of the phase stack, the moves `V → U`,
`E → V` and the decrement of `I`; the recursion at level `i`; `pop_run` restores `SE` and
returns the saved `U` in `E`; the odd phase stack selects `h1`, which halves it back. -/
theorem desc2 (hsw : s ≤ w) (i : ℕ) (hi : i + 1 ≤ w) (IH : CallOK E orc x s w i) (st : St)
    (h : Inv s w (i + 1) st) (hm : st.M < 2 ^ w) (M1 : ℕ) (hM1 : M1 ≤ 2 ^ w) :
    ∃ M2, M2 ≤ 2 ^ w ∧ AReach (A E) orc x (GuardLe (A E) x (2 ^ (w * w)))
      (some (.cp (.push true) 0), St.toV { st with V := st.M, M := M1, E := st.V }, none)
      (some (if decide (Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) i st.M st.V) then .a1T else .a1F),
        St.toV { st with U := st.M, M := M2, E := st.U }, none) := by
  obtain ⟨f1, f2⟩ := size_facts w
  have hbd := h.bd hsw hi
  have hB := hbd
  simp only [St.Bd] at hB
  have hSE1 := push_lt hi h.hSE h.hU
  have hSP1 := pushP_lt hi h.hSP
  have g1 : 2 ^ (w * (w - i)) ≤ 2 ^ (w * w) :=
    Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) (Nat.mul_le_mul_left _ (by omega))
  have g2 : 2 ^ (w - i) ≤ 2 ^ w := Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) (by omega)
  have hle := Nat.le_mul_of_pos_right st.SE (Nat.two_pow_pos w)
  have h3 : Inv s w i
      { st with SE := st.SE * 2 ^ w + st.U, U := st.M, SP := 2 * st.SP + 1, M := M1, I := i } :=
    ⟨h.hn, h.ha, h.hX, h.hP, h.hT, h.hZ, h.hC, h.hQ, h.hE, h.hs, h.hw, h.hK, hm, h.hV,
      hM1, rfl, hSE1, hSP1⟩
  obtain ⟨M2, hM2, hc⟩ := IH _ h3
  dsimp only at hc
  refine ⟨M2, hM2, ?_⟩
  have hw := h.hw
  have hV := h.hV
  have hU := h.hU
  have hSEw : st.SE * 2 ^ st.w = st.SE * 2 ^ w := by rw [hw]
  -- push `(U, 1)`
  refine (pushU_run { st with V := st.M, M := M1, E := st.V } h.hC h.hT h.hZ (by bdt)
    (by show st.SE * 2 ^ st.w + st.U ≤ _; rw [hw]; omega)
    (by show 2 * st.SP ≤ _; omega)).trans ?_
  refine step_of (by bdt) ?_
  regs [astep, A]
  refine (mv_run .a0T1 _ (by bdt) (by regs [mvDst, mvSrc]; omega)).trans ?_
  regs [mvDst, mvSrc, mvExit, zero_add]
  refine (mv_run .a0T2 _ (by bdt) (by regs [mvDst, mvSrc]; omega)).trans ?_
  regs [mvDst, mvSrc, mvExit, zero_add]
  refine step_of (by bdt) ?_
  regs [astep, A]
  refine cont (by ext <;> simp [hw, h.hI, h.hE]) (hc.trans ?_)
  -- `rt b`: not the root, pop the frame
  have hB3 := h3.bd hsw (by omega)
  simp only [St.Bd] at hB3
  refine step_of (by bdt) ?_
  regs [astep, A, if_neg (show i ≠ st.w by omega)]
  refine (pop_run _
    { st with SE := st.SE * 2 ^ w + st.U, U := st.M, SP := 2 * st.SP + 1, M := M2, I := i }
    st.SE st.U h.hC h.hT h.hZ h.hQ h.hE (by bdt) (by simp [hw]) (by simp [hw]; exact hU)).trans ?_
  refine step_of (by bdt) ?_
  regs [astep, A]
  refine step_of (by bdt) ?_
  regs [astep, A, Nat.mul_add_mod, if_true]
  refine step_of (by bdt) ?_
  regs [astep, A]
  refine reach_of_eq (AReach.refl _) ?_
  congr 3
  ext <;> simp [h.hI]
  omega

/-- **The tail after an unreachable first half**: from `a0F`, the machine sets `M := V + 1`,
moves the saved target back into `V`, and returns to `loop`.

**Proof sketch.** A clear, two moves and an increment. -/
theorem tail0F (hsw : s ≤ w) (i : ℕ) (hi : i + 1 ≤ w) (st : St) (h : Inv s w (i + 1) st)
    (hm : st.M < 2 ^ w) (M1 : ℕ) (hM1 : M1 ≤ 2 ^ w) :
    AReach (A E) orc x (GuardLe (A E) x (2 ^ (w * w)))
      (some .a0F, St.toV { st with V := st.M, M := M1, E := st.V }, none)
      (some .loop, St.toV { st with M := st.M + 1 }, none) := by
  obtain ⟨f1, f2⟩ := size_facts w
  have hB := h.bd hsw hi
  simp only [St.Bd] at hB
  have hV := h.hV
  refine step_of (by bdt) ?_
  regs [astep, A]
  refine (mv_run .a0FM _ (by bdt) (by regs [mvDst, mvSrc]; omega)).trans ?_
  regs [mvDst, mvSrc, mvExit, zero_add]
  refine step_of (by bdt) ?_
  regs [astep, A]
  refine reach_of_eq (mv_run .a0FV _ (by bdt) (by regs [mvDst, mvSrc]; omega)) ?_
  regs [mvDst, mvSrc, mvExit, zero_add]
  congr 3
  ext <;> simp [h.hE]

/-- **The tail after a reachable second half**: from `a1T`, the machine moves the saved
source back into `U` and answers `true`.

**Proof sketch.** A clear and a move. -/
theorem tail1T (hsw : s ≤ w) (i : ℕ) (hi : i + 1 ≤ w) (st : St) (h : Inv s w (i + 1) st)
    (M2 : ℕ) (hM2 : M2 ≤ 2 ^ w) :
    AReach (A E) orc x (GuardLe (A E) x (2 ^ (w * w)))
      (some .a1T, St.toV { st with U := st.M, M := M2, E := st.U }, none)
      (some (.rt true), St.toV { st with M := M2 }, none) := by
  obtain ⟨f1, f2⟩ := size_facts w
  have hB := h.bd hsw hi
  simp only [St.Bd] at hB
  have hU := h.hU
  refine step_of (by bdt) ?_
  regs [astep, A]
  refine reach_of_eq (mv_run .a1TU _ (by bdt) (by regs [mvDst, mvSrc]; omega)) ?_
  regs [mvDst, mvSrc, mvExit, zero_add]
  congr 3
  ext <;> simp [h.hE]

/-- **The tail after an unreachable second half**: from `a1F`, the machine sets
`M := U + 1`, moves the saved source back into `U`, and returns to `loop`.

**Proof sketch.** A clear, two moves and an increment. -/
theorem tail1F (hsw : s ≤ w) (i : ℕ) (hi : i + 1 ≤ w) (st : St) (h : Inv s w (i + 1) st)
    (hm : st.M < 2 ^ w) (M2 : ℕ) (hM2 : M2 ≤ 2 ^ w) :
    AReach (A E) orc x (GuardLe (A E) x (2 ^ (w * w)))
      (some .a1F, St.toV { st with U := st.M, M := M2, E := st.U }, none)
      (some .loop, St.toV { st with M := st.M + 1 }, none) := by
  obtain ⟨f1, f2⟩ := size_facts w
  have hB := h.bd hsw hi
  simp only [St.Bd] at hB
  have hU := h.hU
  refine step_of (by bdt) ?_
  regs [astep, A]
  refine (mv_run .a1FM _ (by bdt) (by regs [mvDst, mvSrc]; omega)).trans ?_
  regs [mvDst, mvSrc, mvExit, zero_add]
  refine step_of (by bdt) ?_
  regs [astep, A]
  refine reach_of_eq (mv_run .a1FU _ (by bdt) (by regs [mvDst, mvSrc]; omega)) ?_
  regs [mvDst, mvSrc, mvExit, zero_add]
  congr 3
  ext <;> simp [h.hE]

/-- The invariant does not constrain the midpoint beyond `M ≤ 2 ^ w`. -/
lemma Inv.setM {s w i : ℕ} {st : St} (h : Inv s w i st) {M' : ℕ} (hM : M' ≤ 2 ^ w) :
    Inv s w i { st with M := M' } :=
  ⟨h.hn, h.ha, h.hX, h.hP, h.hT, h.hZ, h.hC, h.hQ, h.hE, h.hs, h.hw, h.hK, h.hU, h.hV, hM,
    h.hI, h.hSE, h.hSP⟩

/-- Skipping a failing candidate does not change a bounded search. -/
lemma exists_shift {R₁ R₂ : ℕ → Prop} {a K : ℕ} (h : ¬ (R₁ a ∧ R₂ a)) :
    (∃ m, a + 1 ≤ m ∧ m < K ∧ R₁ m ∧ R₂ m) ↔ (∃ m, a ≤ m ∧ m < K ∧ R₁ m ∧ R₂ m) := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨m, h1, h2, h3⟩
    exact ⟨m, by omega, h2, h3⟩
  · rintro ⟨m, h1, h2, h3⟩
    rcases Nat.eq_or_lt_of_le h1 with rfl | h1
    · exact absurd h3 h
    · exact ⟨m, h1, h2, h3⟩

open Classical in
/-- **The midpoint loop**: from `loop` at level `i + 1` with midpoint `M`, the machine
answers at `rt b` whether some `m` with `M ≤ m < 2 ^ w` has both halves reachable at level
`i`, changing only `M`.

**Proof sketch.** Induction on `2 ^ w - M`. At `M = 2 ^ w` the machine answers `false`.
Below, the first descent (`desc1`) evaluates the first half; if it fails, `tail0F` moves to
`M + 1`; otherwise the second descent (`desc2`) evaluates the second half, and `tail1T`
answers `true` or `tail1F` moves to `M + 1`. Moving past a failing candidate leaves the
answer unchanged (`exists_shift`). -/
theorem loop_spec (hsw : s ≤ w) (i : ℕ) (hi : i + 1 ≤ w) (IH : CallOK E orc x s w i) :
    ∀ k (st : St), Inv s w (i + 1) st → st.M + k = 2 ^ w → ∃ M', M' ≤ 2 ^ w ∧
      AReach (A E) orc x (GuardLe (A E) x (2 ^ (w * w))) (some .loop, st.toV, none)
        (some (.rt (decide (∃ m, st.M ≤ m ∧ m < 2 ^ w ∧ Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) i st.U m ∧
          Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) i m st.V))), St.toV { st with M := M' }, none) := by
  intro k
  induction k with
  | zero =>
    intro st h hk
    refine ⟨st.M, h.hM, ?_⟩
    refine step_of (h.bd hsw hi) ?_
    regs [astep, A, if_pos (show st.M = st.K by rw [h.hK]; omega)]
    rw [decide_eq_false (by rintro ⟨m, h1, h2, -⟩; omega)]
    exact AReach.refl _
  | succ k ih =>
    intro st h hk
    have hm : st.M < 2 ^ w := by omega
    have hnext := h.setM (M' := st.M + 1) (by omega)
    obtain ⟨M1, hM1, h1⟩ := desc1 hsw i hi IH st h hm
    by_cases r1 : Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) i st.U st.M
    · simp only [r1, decide_true, if_true] at h1
      obtain ⟨M2, hM2, h2⟩ := desc2 hsw i hi IH st h hm M1 hM1
      by_cases r2 : Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) i st.M st.V
      · simp only [r2, decide_true, if_true] at h2
        refine ⟨M2, hM2, ?_⟩
        rw [decide_eq_true ⟨st.M, le_rfl, hm, r1, r2⟩]
        exact h1.trans (h2.trans (tail1T hsw i hi st h M2 hM2))
      · simp only [r2, decide_false, Bool.false_eq_true, if_false] at h2
        obtain ⟨M', hM', h3⟩ := ih _ hnext (by show st.M + 1 + k = 2 ^ w; omega)
        dsimp only at h3
        have e := exists_shift (R₁ := fun m => Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) i st.U m)
          (R₂ := fun m => Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) i m st.V) (a := st.M) (K := 2 ^ w)
          (fun hh => r2 hh.2)
        beta_reduce at e
        rw [decide_eq_decide.mpr e] at h3
        exact ⟨M', hM', h1.trans (h2.trans ((tail1F hsw i hi st h hm M2 hM2).trans h3))⟩
    · simp only [r1, decide_false, Bool.false_eq_true, if_false] at h1
      obtain ⟨M', hM', h3⟩ := ih _ hnext (by show st.M + 1 + k = 2 ^ w; omega)
      dsimp only at h3
      have e := exists_shift (R₁ := fun m => Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) i st.U m)
        (R₂ := fun m => Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) i m st.V) (a := st.M) (K := 2 ^ w)
        (fun hh => r1 hh.1)
      beta_reduce at e
      rw [decide_eq_decide.mpr e] at h3
      exact ⟨M', hM', h1.trans ((tail0F hsw i hi st h hm M1 hM1).trans h3)⟩

/-- **The recursion computes midpoint reachability** [AB09, §4.2.1, proof of
Theorem 4.14]: for every level `i ≤ w`, from `cl` on a register file meeting the invariant at
level `i`, the machine reaches `rt b` with `b` the truth value of `Reach (2 ^ w) R i U V`,
changing only `M` (`CallOK`).

**Proof sketch.** Induction on `i`. Level `0` is `base_spec`. At level `i + 1`, `cl` clears
`M` and enters the midpoint loop (`loop_spec`, using the induction hypothesis for the two
descents); the loop's answer from `M = 0` is `Reach (2 ^ w) R (i + 1) U V` by definition. -/
theorem call_spec (hsw : s ≤ w) : ∀ i, i ≤ w → CallOK E orc x s w i := by
  intro i
  induction i with
  | zero =>
    intro _ st h
    exact ⟨st.M, h.hM, base_spec hsw st h⟩
  | succ i ih =>
    intro hi st h
    have IH := ih (by omega)
    have hbd := h.bd hsw hi
    obtain ⟨M', hM', hl⟩ := loop_spec hsw i hi IH (2 ^ w) _ (h.setM (M' := 0) (Nat.zero_le _))
      (by show 0 + 2 ^ w = 2 ^ w; omega)
    refine ⟨M', hM', ?_⟩
    refine step_of hbd ?_
    regs [astep, A, if_neg (show st.I ≠ 0 by rw [h.hI]; omega)]
    refine step_of hbd ?_
    regs [astep, A]
    dsimp only at hl
    have e : (∃ m, 0 ≤ m ∧ m < 2 ^ w ∧ Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) i st.U m ∧
        Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) i m st.V) ↔ Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) (i + 1) st.U st.V :=
      ⟨fun ⟨m, _, h1, h2⟩ => ⟨m, h1, h2⟩, fun ⟨m, h1, h2⟩ => ⟨m, Nat.zero_le _, h1, h2⟩⟩
    rw [decide_eq_decide.mpr e] at hl
    exact hl

end SavitchARM

end Complexity.LogProg
```

```
/-

Authors: Hydroxyi

import TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.SavitchARM.Setup

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# The outer search of the Savitch register machine

After the setup, `Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.A` runs a register `U` through the codes
below `K = 2 ^ w`, keeping those the initial-code decider accepts, and for each such `U` a
register `V` through the codes the accepting-code decider accepts; for each candidate pair
it evaluates the midpoint recursion at the root level `w`
(`Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.call_spec`) and accepts on success
(`outerV_run`, `outerU_run`). Together with the setup (`setup_run`), the machine answers
whether some initial code reaches some accepting code by midpoint reachability
(`savitch_halts`).

Infrastructure for [AB09, §4.2.1, proof of Theorem 4.14]; not itself a result of the book.

## Main definitions

* `Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt` — the register files of the outer search.
* `Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.InitO`, `AccO` — the code tests read from the oracle, with
  their defining equations `initO_iff_orc`, `accO_iff_orc`.

## Main results

* `Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerU_run` — the outer search.
* `Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt_toV` — the outer search's register files, as registers.
* `Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.savitch_halts` — the whole run.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§4.2.1, Theorem 4.14.)
-/

namespace Complexity.LogProg

namespace SavitchARM

open Turing

/-- **The register files of the outer search**: after the setup, with candidate codes `u`,
`v` and midpoint register `M`. -/
def outerSt (s w u v M : ℕ) : St := { setSt s w with U := u, V := v, M := M }

/-- The initial-code test read from the oracle: decider `1` accepts `⟨x, ⟨bits u, bits s⟩⟩`. -/
def InitO (orc : Fin 4 → List Bool → Bool) (x : List Bool) (s u : ℕ) : Prop :=
  orc 1 (pairEncode x (pairEncode (Nat.bits u) (Nat.bits s))) = true

/-- `InitO orc x s u` holds exactly when decider `1` accepts `⟨x, ⟨bits u, bits s⟩⟩`:
`orc 1 (pairEncode x (pairEncode (bits u) (bits s))) = true`. -/
theorem initO_iff_orc {orc : Fin 4 → List Bool → Bool} {x : List Bool} {s u : ℕ} :
    InitO orc x s u ↔ orc 1 (pairEncode x (pairEncode (Nat.bits u) (Nat.bits s))) = true :=
  Iff.rfl

/-- The accepting-code test read from the oracle: decider `2` accepts
`⟨x, ⟨bits v, bits s⟩⟩`. -/
def AccO (orc : Fin 4 → List Bool → Bool) (x : List Bool) (s v : ℕ) : Prop :=
  orc 2 (pairEncode x (pairEncode (Nat.bits v) (Nat.bits s))) = true

/-- `AccO orc x s v` holds exactly when decider `2` accepts `⟨x, ⟨bits v, bits s⟩⟩`:
`orc 2 (pairEncode x (pairEncode (bits v) (bits s))) = true`. -/
theorem accO_iff_orc {orc : Fin 4 → List Bool → Bool} {x : List Bool} {s v : ℕ} :
    AccO orc x s v ↔ orc 2 (pairEncode x (pairEncode (Nat.bits v) (Nat.bits s))) = true :=
  Iff.rfl

section Outer

variable {s w u v M : ℕ}

/-- The `U` register of an outer-search file. -/
@[simp] lemma outerSt_U : (outerSt s w u v M).U = u := rfl
/-- The `V` register of an outer-search file. -/
@[simp] lemma outerSt_V : (outerSt s w u v M).V = v := rfl
/-- The `M` register of an outer-search file. -/
@[simp] lemma outerSt_M : (outerSt s w u v M).M = M := rfl
/-- The `I` register of an outer-search file. -/
@[simp] lemma outerSt_I : (outerSt s w u v M).I = 0 := rfl
/-- The `K` register of an outer-search file. -/
@[simp] lemma outerSt_K : (outerSt s w u v M).K = 2 ^ w := rfl
/-- The `w` register of an outer-search file. -/
@[simp] lemma outerSt_w : (outerSt s w u v M).w = w := rfl
/-- The `s` register of an outer-search file. -/
@[simp] lemma outerSt_s : (outerSt s w u v M).s = s := rfl

/-- **The outer search's register files, as registers**: the setup's file with the candidate
registers `U`, `V` and `M` written. -/
theorem outerSt_toV (s w u v M : ℕ) : (outerSt s w u v M).toV =
    Function.update (Function.update (Function.update (setSt s w).toV rU u) rV v) rM M := by
  rw [St.upd_U, St.upd_V, St.upd_M]
  rfl

/-- The register files of the outer search are bounded by `2 ^ (w · w)`. -/
lemma outerSt_bd (hsw : s ≤ w) (hu : u ≤ 2 ^ w) (hv : v ≤ 2 ^ w) (hM : M ≤ 2 ^ w) :
    (outerSt s w u v M).Bd (2 ^ (w * w)) := by
  obtain ⟨f1, f2⟩ := size_facts w
  simp only [St.Bd, outerSt, setSt, St.zero]
  omega

/-- The register files of the outer search, with the level set to `w`, meet the invariant
of the root level. -/
lemma outerSt_inv (hu : u < 2 ^ w) (hv : v < 2 ^ w) (hM : M ≤ 2 ^ w) :
    Inv s w w { outerSt s w u v M with I := w } :=
  ⟨rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl, hu, hv, hM, rfl,
    by simp [outerSt, setSt, St.zero], by simp [outerSt, setSt, St.zero]⟩

end Outer

variable {E : ℕ} {orc : Fin 4 → List Bool → Bool} {x : List Bool} {s w : ℕ}

open Classical in
/-- **The inner search**: from `OV` with candidate initial code `u` and counter `v`, the
machine answers whether some accepting code `v' ∈ [v, 2 ^ w)` has
`Reach (2 ^ w) R w u v'`, and otherwise continues as from `NU` (answering `b₀`).

**Proof sketch.** Induction on `2 ^ w - v`. At `v = 2 ^ w` the machine clears `V` and goes
to `NU`. Below, it asks decider `2` about `v`; on acceptance it sets `I := w` and runs the
recursion (`call_spec`), accepting if it answers `true`; otherwise it moves to `v + 1`. -/
theorem outerV_run (hsw : s ≤ w) (u : ℕ) (hu : u < 2 ^ w) (b₀ : Bool)
    (hNU : ∀ M ≤ 2 ^ w, AHalt (A E) orc x (GuardLe (A E) x (2 ^ (w * w)))
      (some .NU, (outerSt s w u 0 M).toV, none) b₀) :
    ∀ k v M, v + k = 2 ^ w → M ≤ 2 ^ w →
      AHalt (A E) orc x (GuardLe (A E) x (2 ^ (w * w))) (some .OV, (outerSt s w u v M).toV, none)
        (decide (∃ v', v ≤ v' ∧ v' < 2 ^ w ∧ AccO orc x s v' ∧
          Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) w u v') || b₀) := by
  intro k
  induction k with
  | zero =>
    intro v M hk hM
    have hbd := outerSt_bd hsw hu.le (le_of_eq (by omega)) hM
    refine AHalt.step (gb_of hbd _) ?_
    regs [astep, A, outerSt_V, outerSt_K, if_pos (show v = 2 ^ w by omega)]
    refine AHalt.step (gb_of hbd _) ?_
    regs [astep, A]
    rw [decide_eq_false (by rintro ⟨v', h1, h2, -⟩; omega), Bool.false_or]
    exact hNU M hM
  | succ k ih =>
    intro v M hk hM
    have hv : v < 2 ^ w := by omega
    have hbd := outerSt_bd hsw hu.le hv.le hM
    obtain ⟨f1, f2⟩ := size_facts w
    have shift : ∀ (hn : ¬ (AccO orc x s v ∧ Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) w u v)) (M' : ℕ),
        M' ≤ 2 ^ w → AHalt (A E) orc x (GuardLe (A E) x (2 ^ (w * w)))
          (some .NV, (outerSt s w u v M').toV, none)
          (decide (∃ v', v ≤ v' ∧ v' < 2 ^ w ∧ AccO orc x s v' ∧
            Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) w u v') || b₀) := by
      intro hn M' hM'
      refine AHalt.step (gb_of (outerSt_bd hsw hu.le hv.le hM') _) ?_
      regs [astep, A, outerSt_V]
      have e := exists_shift (R₁ := fun m => AccO orc x s m)
        (R₂ := fun m => Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) w u m) (a := v) (K := 2 ^ w) hn
      beta_reduce at e
      rw [← decide_eq_decide.mpr e]
      exact ih (v + 1) M' (by omega) hM'
    refine AHalt.step (gb_of hbd _) ?_
    regs [astep, A, outerSt_V, outerSt_K, if_neg (show v ≠ 2 ^ w by omega)]
    refine AHalt.step (gb_of hbd _) ?_
    simp only [astep, A, vword_whole₂]
    regs [outerSt_V, outerSt_s]
    by_cases ha : AccO orc x s v
    · have ha' : orc 2 (pairEncode x (pairEncode (Nat.bits v) (Nat.bits s))) = true := ha
      rw [if_pos ha']
      -- `root`: set `I := w` and run the recursion
      refine AHalt.step (gb_of hbd _) ?_
      regs [astep, A]
      refine (cp_run .rootW _ (by simp only [St.Bd, outerSt, setSt, St.zero]; omega) rfl
        (by regs [cpDst, cpSrc]; simp only [outerSt, setSt, St.zero]; omega)).halt ?_
      regs [cpDst, cpSrc, cpExit]
      obtain ⟨M', hM', hc⟩ := call_spec (E := E) (orc := orc) (x := x) hsw w le_rfl _
        (outerSt_inv (s := s) hu hv hM)
      refine contH (st' := { outerSt s w u v M with I := w }) (by ext <;> simp [outerSt, setSt,
        St.zero]) (hc.halt ?_)
      dsimp only
      have hbd' : St.Bd (2 ^ (w * w)) { outerSt s w u v M' with I := w } := by
        simp only [St.Bd, outerSt, setSt, St.zero]; omega
      refine AHalt.step (gb_of hbd' _) ?_
      regs [astep, A, outerSt_U, outerSt_V, outerSt_w, if_true]
      by_cases hr : Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) w u v
      · simp only [hr, decide_true, ↓reduceIte]
        rw [decide_eq_true ⟨v, le_rfl, hv, ha, hr⟩, Bool.true_or]
        exact AHalt.ret rfl (gb_of hbd' _)
      · simp only [hr, decide_false, Bool.false_eq_true, ↓reduceIte]
        refine AHalt.step (gb_of hbd' _) ?_
        regs [astep, A]
        exact shift (fun hh => hr hh.2) M' hM'
    · have ha' : ¬ orc 2 (pairEncode x (pairEncode (Nat.bits v) (Nat.bits s))) = true := ha
      rw [if_neg ha']
      exact shift (fun hh => ha hh.1) M hM

open Classical in
/-- **The outer search**: from `OU` with candidate `u` (and `V = 0`), the machine answers
whether some initial code `u' ∈ [u, 2 ^ w)` reaches some accepting code `v < 2 ^ w` by
midpoint reachability at level `w`.

**Proof sketch.** Induction on `2 ^ w - u`. At `u = 2 ^ w` the machine rejects. Below, it
asks decider `1` about `u`; on acceptance it runs the inner search (`outerV_run`), which
falls through to `u + 1` (the induction hypothesis, through `NU`); otherwise it moves to
`u + 1` directly. -/
theorem outerU_run (hsw : s ≤ w) : ∀ k u M, u + k = 2 ^ w → M ≤ 2 ^ w →
    AHalt (A E) orc x (GuardLe (A E) x (2 ^ (w * w))) (some .OU, (outerSt s w u 0 M).toV, none)
      (decide (∃ u', u ≤ u' ∧ u' < 2 ^ w ∧ InitO orc x s u' ∧
        ∃ v < 2 ^ w, AccO orc x s v ∧ Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) w u' v)) := by
  intro k
  induction k with
  | zero =>
    intro u M hk hM
    have hbd := outerSt_bd hsw (le_of_eq (by omega)) (Nat.zero_le _) hM
    refine AHalt.step (gb_of hbd _) ?_
    regs [astep, A, outerSt_U, outerSt_K, if_pos (show u = 2 ^ w by omega)]
    rw [decide_eq_false (by rintro ⟨u', h1, h2, -⟩; omega)]
    exact AHalt.ret rfl (gb_of hbd _)
  | succ k ih =>
    intro u M hk hM
    have hu : u < 2 ^ w := by omega
    have hbd := outerSt_bd hsw hu.le (Nat.zero_le _) hM
    have hNU : ∀ M' ≤ 2 ^ w, AHalt (A E) orc x (GuardLe (A E) x (2 ^ (w * w)))
        (some .NU, (outerSt s w u 0 M').toV, none)
        (decide (∃ u', u + 1 ≤ u' ∧ u' < 2 ^ w ∧ InitO orc x s u' ∧
          ∃ v < 2 ^ w, AccO orc x s v ∧ Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) w u' v)) := by
      intro M' hM'
      refine AHalt.step (gb_of (outerSt_bd hsw hu.le (Nat.zero_le _) hM') _) ?_
      regs [astep, A, outerSt_U]
      exact ih (u + 1) M' (by omega) hM'
    refine AHalt.step (gb_of hbd _) ?_
    regs [astep, A, outerSt_U, outerSt_K, if_neg (show u ≠ 2 ^ w by omega)]
    refine AHalt.step (gb_of hbd _) ?_
    simp only [astep, A, vword_whole₂]
    regs [outerSt_U, outerSt_s]
    by_cases hi : InitO orc x s u
    · have hi' : orc 1 (pairEncode x (pairEncode (Nat.bits u) (Nat.bits s))) = true := hi
      rw [if_pos hi']
      have h := outerV_run hsw u hu _ hNU (2 ^ w) 0 M (by omega) hM
      have e : decide (∃ u', u ≤ u' ∧ u' < 2 ^ w ∧ InitO orc x s u' ∧
          ∃ v < 2 ^ w, AccO orc x s v ∧ Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) w u' v) =
          (decide (∃ v', 0 ≤ v' ∧ v' < 2 ^ w ∧ AccO orc x s v' ∧
            Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) w u v') ||
          decide (∃ u', u + 1 ≤ u' ∧ u' < 2 ^ w ∧ InitO orc x s u' ∧
            ∃ v < 2 ^ w, AccO orc x s v ∧ Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) w u' v)) := by
        rw [Bool.eq_iff_iff]
        simp only [Bool.or_eq_true, decide_eq_true_eq]
        constructor
        · rintro ⟨u', h1, h2, h3, v, hv, h4, h5⟩
          rcases Nat.eq_or_lt_of_le h1 with rfl | h1
          · exact Or.inl ⟨v, Nat.zero_le _, hv, h4, h5⟩
          · exact Or.inr ⟨u', h1, h2, h3, v, hv, h4, h5⟩
        · rintro (⟨v, -, hv, h4, h5⟩ | ⟨u', h1, h2, h3, h4⟩)
          · exact ⟨u, le_rfl, hu, hi, v, hv, h4, h5⟩
          · exact ⟨u', by omega, h2, h3, h4⟩
      rw [e]
      exact h
    · have hi' : ¬ orc 1 (pairEncode x (pairEncode (Nat.bits u) (Nat.bits s))) = true := hi
      rw [if_neg hi']
      have e := exists_shift (R₁ := fun m => InitO orc x s m)
        (R₂ := fun m => ∃ v < 2 ^ w, AccO orc x s v ∧ Reach (2 ^ w) (Rel orc x s) w m v)
        (a := u) (K := 2 ^ w) (fun hh => hi hh.1)
      beta_reduce at e
      rw [← decide_eq_decide.mpr e]
      exact hNU M hM

open Classical in
/-- **The run of the Savitch machine** [AB09, §4.2.1, proof of Theorem 4.14]: with
`n = |x|`, `s = (n + 2) ^ E` and `w = (n + 2) ^ (2E)`, the machine `A E` (with `E ≥ 1`),
started with all registers clear and decider `0` answering length queries, answers whether
some initial code `u < 2 ^ w` reaches some accepting code `v < 2 ^ w` by midpoint
reachability at level `w`, through register values at most `2 ^ (w · w)`.

**Proof sketch.** `setup_run` followed by `outerU_run` from `u = 0`. -/
theorem savitch_halts (hE : 1 ≤ E)
    (hq : ∀ k ≤ x.length, orc 0 (pairEncode x (Nat.bits k)) = decide (k < x.length)) :
    AHalt (A E) orc x (GuardLe (A E) x (2 ^ ((x.length + 2) ^ (2 * E) * (x.length + 2) ^ (2 * E))))
      (some .scan, fun _ => 0, none)
      (decide (∃ u < 2 ^ (x.length + 2) ^ (2 * E), InitO orc x ((x.length + 2) ^ E) u ∧
        ∃ v < 2 ^ (x.length + 2) ^ (2 * E), AccO orc x ((x.length + 2) ^ E) v ∧
          Reach (2 ^ (x.length + 2) ^ (2 * E)) (Rel orc x ((x.length + 2) ^ E))
            ((x.length + 2) ^ (2 * E)) u v)) := by
  have hsw : (x.length + 2) ^ E ≤ (x.length + 2) ^ (2 * E) :=
    Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by omega) (by omega)
  obtain ⟨-, f2⟩ := size_facts ((x.length + 2) ^ (2 * E))
  rw [St.toV_zero]
  refine (setup_run hE hq f2).halt ?_
  have h := outerU_run (E := E) (orc := orc) (x := x) hsw _ 0 0 (zero_add _) (Nat.zero_le _)
  have e : (∃ u', 0 ≤ u' ∧ u' < 2 ^ (x.length + 2) ^ (2 * E) ∧
      InitO orc x ((x.length + 2) ^ E) u' ∧
      ∃ v < 2 ^ (x.length + 2) ^ (2 * E), AccO orc x ((x.length + 2) ^ E) v ∧
        Reach (2 ^ (x.length + 2) ^ (2 * E)) (Rel orc x ((x.length + 2) ^ E))
          ((x.length + 2) ^ (2 * E)) u' v) ↔
      ∃ u < 2 ^ (x.length + 2) ^ (2 * E), InitO orc x ((x.length + 2) ^ E) u ∧
        ∃ v < 2 ^ (x.length + 2) ^ (2 * E), AccO orc x ((x.length + 2) ^ E) v ∧
          Reach (2 ^ (x.length + 2) ^ (2 * E)) (Rel orc x ((x.length + 2) ^ E))
            ((x.length + 2) ^ (2 * E)) u v :=
    ⟨fun ⟨u, _, h1, h2⟩ => ⟨u, h1, h2⟩, fun ⟨u, h1, h2⟩ => ⟨u, Nat.zero_le _, h1, h2⟩⟩
  rw [decide_eq_decide.mpr e] at h
  exact h

end SavitchARM

end Complexity.LogProg
```

## ===== TCSlib/Complexity/SpaceComplexity/SavitchARM/Setup.lean =====

```
/-
Copyright (c) 2026 TCSlib contributors. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Hydroxyi
-/
import TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.SavitchARM.Recursion

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# The setup and the outer search of the Savitch register machine

The non-recursive parts of `Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.A`. The setup (`setup_run`)
measures the input, computes the radius `s = (|x| + 2) ^ E`, the width
`w = (|x| + 2) ^ (2E)` and the code bound `K = 2 ^ w` by counting loops, leaving every other
register clear. The outer search (`outerU_run`, `outerV_run`) runs through the candidate
initial codes `U < K` and accepting codes `V < K` and evaluates the midpoint recursion at the
root level `w` for each candidate pair (`Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.call_spec`).

Infrastructure for [AB09, §4.2.1, proof of Theorem 4.14]; not itself a result of the book.

## Main definitions

* `Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerSt` — the register files of the outer search.

## Main results

* `Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.setup_run` — the setup.
* `Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.setSt_toV` — the register file after the setup, as registers.
* `Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.outerU_run` — the outer search answers whether an initial
  and an accepting code are joined by midpoint reachability at level `w`.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§4.2.1, Theorem 4.14.)
-/

namespace Complexity.LogProg

namespace SavitchARM

open Turing

variable {E : ℕ} {orc : Fin 4 → List Bool → Bool} {x : List Bool} {B : ℕ}

/-! ## The setup -/

/-- Close a bound on a named register file, reducing its projections first. -/
scoped macro "sbd" : tactic =>
  `(tactic| ((try simp only [St.Bd, St.zero]) <;> (try dsimp only) <;>
    (try simp only [one_mul, zero_add, if_true, ↓reduceIte]) <;> omega))

/-- **Loading the constant `E`**: from `ld j` with `X = j`, the machine counts `X` up to `E`,
then sets `P := P + 1` and reaches `pw`.

**Proof sketch.** Induction on `E - j`. -/
theorem ld_run : ∀ (k j : ℕ) (hj : j < E + 1) (st : St), j + k = E → st.X = j → st.Bd B →
    E ≤ B → st.P + 1 ≤ B →
    AReach (A E) orc x (GuardLe (A E) x B) (some (.ld ⟨j, hj⟩), st.toV, none)
      (some .pw, St.toV { st with X := E, P := st.P + 1 }, none) := by
  intro k
  induction k with
  | zero =>
    intro j hj st hk hX hbd hE hP
    refine step_of hbd ?_
    regs [astep, A, dif_neg (show ¬ j < E by omega)]
    refine reach_of_eq (AReach.refl _) ?_
    congr 3
    ext <;> simp; omega
  | succ k ih =>
    intro j hj st hk hX hbd hE hP
    refine step_of hbd ?_
    regs [astep, A, dif_pos (show j < E by omega)]
    have hbd1 : St.Bd B { st with X := st.X + 1 } := by simp only [St.Bd] at hbd ⊢; omega
    refine reach_of_eq (ih (j + 1) (by omega) _ (by omega) (by simp [hX]) hbd1 hE hP) ?_
    rfl

/-- **The power loop**: from `pw` with `X = j` and `C = T = Z = 0`, the machine multiplies
`P` by `a ^ j`, clears `X`, and reaches `cp sP`.

**Proof sketch.** Induction on `j`: each round decrements `X` and multiplies `P` by `a`
(`mul_run`). -/
theorem pw_run : ∀ (j : ℕ) (st : St), st.X = j → st.C = 0 → st.T = 0 → st.Z = 0 → st.Bd B →
    1 ≤ st.a → st.P * st.a ^ j ≤ B →
    AReach (A E) orc x (GuardLe (A E) x B) (some .pw, st.toV, none)
      (some (.cp .sP 0), St.toV { st with X := 0, P := st.P * st.a ^ j }, none) := by
  intro j
  induction j with
  | zero =>
    intro st hX hC hT hZ hbd ha hb
    refine step_of hbd ?_
    regs [astep, A, hX, if_true]
    refine reach_of_eq (AReach.refl _) ?_
    congr 3
    ext <;> simp [hX]
  | succ j ih =>
    intro st hX hC hT hZ hbd ha hb
    have h1 : st.P ≤ st.P * st.a ^ (j + 1) :=
      Nat.le_mul_of_pos_right _ (Nat.pow_pos (by omega))
    have h2 : st.P * st.a ≤ st.P * st.a ^ (j + 1) := by
      apply Nat.mul_le_mul_left
      calc st.a = st.a ^ 1 := (pow_one _).symm
        _ ≤ st.a ^ (j + 1) := Nat.pow_le_pow_right ha (by omega)
    refine step_of hbd ?_
    regs [astep, A, hX, Nat.add_one_ne_zero, if_false]
    refine step_of hbd ?_
    regs [astep, A, hX, Nat.add_sub_cancel]
    have hbd1 : St.Bd B { st with X := j } := by simp only [St.Bd] at hbd ⊢; omega
    refine (mul_run false { st with X := j } hC hT hZ hbd1 (by simp; omega)).trans ?_
    simp only [mvExit, Bool.false_eq_true, if_false]
    have hbd2 : St.Bd B { st with X := j, P := st.P * st.a } := by
      simp only [St.Bd] at hbd ⊢; omega
    refine reach_of_eq (ih _ rfl hC hT hZ hbd2 ha (by
      show st.P * st.a * st.a ^ j ≤ B
      rw [mul_assoc, ← pow_succ']; exact hb)) ?_
    congr 3
    ext <;> simp [pow_succ']
    ring

/-- **The register file after the setup**: radius `s`, width `w`, code bound `2 ^ w`, every
other register clear. -/
def setSt (s w : ℕ) : St := { St.zero with s := s, w := w, K := 2 ^ w }

/-- **The register file after the setup, as registers**: `s`, `w` and `2 ^ w` in the radius,
width and code-bound registers, every other register clear. -/
theorem setSt_toV (s w : ℕ) : (setSt s w).toV =
    Function.update (Function.update (Function.update (fun _ => 0) rs s) rw w) rK (2 ^ w) := by
  rw [St.toV_zero, St.upd_s, St.upd_w, St.upd_K]
  rfl

/-- **The setup** [AB09, §4.2.1: the radius and the vertex-code width are computed first]:
from `scan` with all registers clear, the machine reaches `OU` with radius
`s = (|x| + 2) ^ E`, width `w = (|x| + 2) ^ (2E)` and code bound `2 ^ w`, everything else
clear, through register values at most `B ≥ 2 ^ w`.

**Proof sketch.** Count `n = |x|` (`Complexity.LogProg.inputLength_loop`, asking decider `0`),
move it into `a` and add two, load `X = E` and `P = 1` (`ld_run`), take `P := a ^ E`
(`pw_run`), copy it into `s`, square `P` (`mul_run`), move it into `w`, clear `a`, and shift
`K = 1` left by `w` (`sh_run`). -/
theorem setup_run (hE : 1 ≤ E)
    (hq : ∀ k ≤ x.length, orc 0 (pairEncode x (Nat.bits k)) = decide (k < x.length))
    (hB : 2 ^ ((x.length + 2) ^ (2 * E)) ≤ B) :
    AReach (A E) orc x (GuardLe (A E) x B) (some .scan, St.zero.toV, none)
      (some .OU, (setSt ((x.length + 2) ^ E) ((x.length + 2) ^ (2 * E))).toV, none) := by
  have hw1 : (x.length + 2) ^ (2 * E) < 2 ^ ((x.length + 2) ^ (2 * E)) := Nat.lt_two_pow_self
  have haE : x.length + 2 ≤ (x.length + 2) ^ E := by
    calc x.length + 2 = (x.length + 2) ^ 1 := (pow_one _).symm
      _ ≤ (x.length + 2) ^ E := Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by omega) hE
  have hEw : (x.length + 2) ^ E ≤ (x.length + 2) ^ (2 * E) :=
    Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by omega) (by omega)
  have hsq : (x.length + 2) ^ E * (x.length + 2) ^ E = (x.length + 2) ^ (2 * E) := by
    rw [← pow_add]; ring_nf
  have hEa : E < (x.length + 2) ^ E :=
    (Nat.lt_two_pow_self).trans_le (Nat.pow_le_pow_left (by omega) _)
  -- count `n = |x|`
  have h1 := inputLength_loop (A E) orc x rn 0 .scan .incN (.mv .aN 0) rfl rfl hq B
    (by omega) St.zero.toV (fun r => by fin_cases r <;> simp [St.toV, St.zero])
    (by simp [St.zero])
  refine (h1.mono fun _ h => h).trans ?_
  regs [St.zero]
  refine (mv_run .aN _ (by sbd) (by regs [mvDst, mvSrc]; omega)).trans ?_
  regs [mvDst, mvSrc, mvExit, zero_add]
  refine step_of (by sbd) ?_
  regs [astep, A]
  refine step_of (by sbd) ?_
  regs [astep, A]
  refine cont (st' := { St.zero with a := x.length + 2 }) (by ext <;> simp [St.zero]) ?_
  -- load `X = E`, `P = 1`
  refine (ld_run E 0 (by omega) _ (by omega) rfl (by sbd) (by omega) (by sbd)).trans ?_
  -- `P := a ^ E`
  refine (pw_run E _ rfl rfl rfl rfl (by sbd) (by sbd) (by sbd)).trans ?_
  -- `s := P`, `P := P · P`, `w := P`
  refine (cp_run .sP _ (by sbd) rfl (by regs [cpDst, cpSrc]; sbd)).trans ?_
  regs [cpDst, cpSrc, cpExit, zero_add, one_mul]
  refine (mul_run true _ rfl rfl rfl (by sbd) (by sbd)).trans ?_
  simp only [mvExit, if_true]
  refine (mv_run .wP _ (by sbd) (by regs [mvDst, mvSrc]; sbd)).trans ?_
  regs [mvDst, mvSrc, mvExit, zero_add]
  refine step_of (by sbd) ?_
  regs [astep, A]
  refine step_of (by sbd) ?_
  regs [astep, A, zero_add]
  -- `K := 2 ^ w`
  refine (cp_run .kW _ (by sbd) rfl (by regs [cpDst, cpSrc]; sbd)).trans ?_
  regs [cpDst, cpSrc, cpExit, zero_add]
  refine reach_of_eq (sh_run .kK _ (by sbd) rfl
    (by regs [shReg]; simp only [St.zero, zero_add, one_mul, hsq]; omega)) ?_
  regs [shReg, shExit]
  congr 3
  ext <;> simp [setSt, St.zero, hsq]

end SavitchARM

end Complexity.LogProg
```

## ===== TCSlib/Complexity/SpaceComplexity/SavitchARM/Window.lean =====

```
/-
Copyright (c) 2026 Seyoon Ragavan. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Seyoon Ragavan
-/
import TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.SavitchARM.Reach
import TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.ExpBFS.Radius

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Windows without a known space bound

Savitch's search (`TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.SavitchARM.Reach`) decides membership by
midpoint reachability over the configuration codes at a radius `s` that bounds the decider's
space, `sp |x| ≤ s` (`Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.mem_iff_reach`). When the space bound is not
computable, the radius is found by iterative deepening: at `s = 1, 2, …`, ask whether some
configuration with a work head on the window's edge (`±s`) is reachable. This file proves the two
facts the deepening needs:

* **window exactness** (`mem_iff_reach_of_noEdge`): if no edge code is reachable at radius `s`,
  membership is midpoint reachability at radius `s`, whatever the space bound. Every run then
  keeps its heads strictly inside the window, so it never leaves it;
* **termination** (`noEdge_of_lt`): beyond the space bound, no edge code is reachable.

Reachability of codes is that of `Complexity.ExpBFS.RCode`, whose codes are those of the
window runs (`Complexity.ExpBFS.rcode_iff`); a path through codes below `2 ^ w` is a midpoint
witness at level `w` (`Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.reach_of_reflTransGen`).

The deepening is that of [Sip13, §8.1, proof of Theorem 8.5]: when the space bound is not
known, try the bounds `1, 2, …`; at each, test acceptance and test whether any configuration one
cell longer is reachable, and reject once none is. This is configuration-graph infrastructure for
Savitch's theorem without space constructibility (cf. [AB09, §4.2.1, Theorem 4.14], which assumes
`S` space-constructible and computes the radius instead).

## Main definitions

* `Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.NoEdge` — no edge code is reachable at radius `s`, level `w`,
  with its defining equation `noEdge_iff`.

## Main results

* `Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.mem_iff_reach_of_noEdge` — window exactness.
* `Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.noEdge_of_lt` — termination.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§4.1.1; §4.2.1, Theorem 4.14.)
* [Sip13] M. Sipser, *Introduction to the Theory of Computation*, 3rd ed., Cengage Learning,
  2013. (§8.1, the proof of Theorem 8.5, Savitch's theorem: the space bound found by trying
  `1, 2, …`.)
-/

namespace Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM

open Turing Codec

variable {N : FinNDTM Bool} {x : List Bool}

/-- **No reachable edge code**: no code `v < 2 ^ w` of a configuration with a work head at `±s`
(a member of `Complexity.Codec.edgeLang`) is a midpoint-reachability target, at level `w`, of an
initial code `u < 2 ^ w`, at radius `s`. -/
def NoEdge (N : FinNDTM Bool) (x : List Bool) (s w : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ¬ ∃ u < 2 ^ w, pairEncode x (pairEncode (Nat.bits u) (Nat.bits s)) ∈ initLang N ∧
    ∃ v < 2 ^ w, pairEncode x (pairEncode (Nat.bits v) (Nat.bits s)) ∈ edgeLang N ∧
      Reach (2 ^ w) (StepRel N x s) w u v

/-- `NoEdge N x s w` holds exactly when there are no `u < 2 ^ w` and `v < 2 ^ w` such that
`⟨x, ⟨bits u, bits s⟩⟩` is in `Complexity.Codec.initLang N`, `⟨x, ⟨bits v, bits s⟩⟩` is in
`Complexity.Codec.edgeLang N`, and `Reach (2 ^ w) (StepRel N x s) w u v` holds. -/
theorem noEdge_iff {s w : ℕ} :
    NoEdge N x s w ↔
      ¬ ∃ u < 2 ^ w, pairEncode x (pairEncode (Nat.bits u) (Nat.bits s)) ∈ initLang N ∧
        ∃ v < 2 ^ w, pairEncode x (pairEncode (Nat.bits v) (Nat.bits s)) ∈ edgeLang N ∧
          Reach (2 ^ w) (StepRel N x s) w u v :=
  Iff.rfl

/-- Codes at radius `s` lie below `2 ^ w` once `w` is at least the code width. -/
private theorem window_code_lt {s w : ℕ} (hw : codeK N * (s + logSpace x.length + 1) ≤ w)
    (C : Cfg N.k Bool N.State x) : cfgCode s C < 2 ^ w :=
  (cfgCode_lt s C).trans_le (Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) hw)

/-- A reachable code is a midpoint witness from the initial code at level `w`, once `w` is at
least the code width. -/
private theorem window_reach_of_rcode {s w v : ℕ}
    (hw : codeK N * (s + logSpace x.length + 1) ≤ w) (h : ExpBFS.RCode N x s v) :
    Reach (2 ^ w) (StepRel N x s) w (cfgCode s (N.tm.initCfg x)) v := by
  refine reach_of_reflTransGen _ _ (fun a b hab => ?_) (window_code_lt hw _)
    (ExpBFS.rcode_iff_reflTransGen.mp h) w le_rfl
  obtain ⟨C, -, rfl, C', -, -, rfl⟩ := (mem_stepLang N x a b s).mp (stepRel_iff_mem.mp hab)
  exact ⟨window_code_lt hw C, window_code_lt hw C'⟩

/-- **Termination** ([Sip13, §8.1, proof of Theorem 8.5]; cf. [AB09, §4.1.1]): if `N` decides
`L` in space `sp` and `sp |x| < s`, no edge code is reachable at radius `s`, at any level.

**Proof sketch.** A midpoint witness is a path of step pairs (`reflTransGen_of_reach`), so its
end is a reachable code, the code of some window run (`Complexity.ExpBFS.rcode_iff`). An edge
configuration with that code has the run's vertex (`Complexity.ExpBFS.coreSum_eq_of_code_eq`),
and every run of `N` lies in the window `sp |x|`
(`Complexity.ExpBFS.inWin_runWith_of_decides`), so its heads are within `sp |x| < s`
(`Turing.NDTM.inWindow_of_coreSum_eq`, `Turing.Cfg.InWindow.core_bounds`): none is at `±s`. -/
theorem noEdge_of_lt {L : Language Bool} {sp : ℕ → ℕ} (h : N.DecidesInSpace L sp)
    (x : List Bool) (s w : ℕ) (hs : sp x.length < s) : NoEdge N x s w := by
  rintro ⟨u, -, hu, v, -, hv, hr⟩
  rw [mem_initLang] at hu
  subst hu
  obtain ⟨C, hC, hcC, i, hi⟩ := (mem_edgeLang N x v s).mp hv
  have hrc : ExpBFS.RCode N x s v :=
    ExpBFS.rcode_iff_reflTransGen.mpr (reflTransGen_of_reach _ _ w _ v hr)
  obtain ⟨w', hw', hcode⟩ := (ExpBFS.rcode_iff s v).mp hrc
  have hcore := ExpBFS.coreSum_eq_of_code_eq hC hw'.last (hcC.trans hcode.symm)
  have hCw : Cfg.InWindow (sp x.length) C :=
    NDTM.inWindow_of_coreSum_eq hcore (ExpBFS.inWin_runWith_of_decides h w')
  have hb := ((Cfg.InWindow.core_bounds hCw) i).1
  rw [hi] at hb
  exact absurd (by exact_mod_cast hb : s ≤ sp x.length) (not_le.mpr hs)

/-- **Window exactness** ([Sip13, §8.1, proof of Theorem 8.5]; cf. [AB09, §4.2.1, proof of
Theorem 4.14]): let `N` decide `L` in space `sp`,
and let `w` be at least the code width at radius `s`. If no edge code is reachable at radius `s`
(`NoEdge`), then `x ∈ L` iff some initial code `u < 2 ^ w` and some accepting code `v < 2 ^ w`
have `Reach (2 ^ w) (StepRel N x s) w u v`. Unlike `mem_iff_reach`, neither a bound
`sp |x| ≤ s` nor a configuration-count bound is assumed.

**Proof sketch.** (⇒) Take an accepting branch (`DecidesInSpace.mem_iff_acceptsWithin_configBound`).
By induction on its prefixes, each is a window run at `s` (`Complexity.ExpBFS.WinRun`): the
current configuration's code is reachable (`Complexity.ExpBFS.rcode_iff`), hence a midpoint
witness (`reach_of_reflTransGen`), so by `NoEdge` it is not an edge code and its heads are strictly
inside `[-s, s]`; one more step then stays in the window (`Turing.Cfg.InWindow.apply_of_lt`,
through `Complexity.Codec.stepWith_eq_apply`). The last configuration is accepting and its code is
reachable. (⇐) Unfold the witness into a path (`reflTransGen_of_reach`) and realize it by a
branch (`Complexity.Codec.mem_of_codePath`). -/
theorem mem_iff_reach_of_noEdge {L : Language Bool} {sp : ℕ → ℕ}
    (h : N.DecidesInSpace L sp) (x : List Bool) (s w : ℕ)
    (hw : codeK N * (s + logSpace x.length + 1) ≤ w) (hne : NoEdge N x s w) :
    x ∈ L ↔ ∃ u < 2 ^ w, pairEncode x (pairEncode (Nat.bits u) (Nat.bits s)) ∈ initLang N ∧
      ∃ v < 2 ^ w, pairEncode x (pairEncode (Nat.bits v) (Nat.bits s)) ∈ acceptLang N ∧
        Reach (2 ^ w) (StepRel N x s) w u v := by
  constructor
  · intro hx
    obtain ⟨wd, -, hhalt, hout⟩ :=
      FinNDTM.acceptsWithin_iff.mp ((h.mem_iff_acceptsWithin_configBound x).mp hx)
    have key : ∀ j ≤ wd.length, ExpBFS.WinRun N x s (wd.take j) := by
      intro j
      induction j with
      | zero =>
        intro _
        refine ExpBFS.winRun_iff.mpr fun i _ => ?_
        rw [List.take_zero, List.take_nil, NDTM.runWith_nil]
        exact ExpBFS.inWin_init s
      | succ j ih =>
        intro hj
        have hW := ih (by omega)
        have hlt : ∀ i,
            |(N.tm.runWith (wd.take j) (N.tm.initCfg x)).workTapePos i| < (s : ℤ) := by
          intro i
          rcases lt_or_eq_of_le ((Cfg.InWindow.core_bounds hW.last) i).1 with h1 | h1
          · exact h1
          · exfalso
            exact hne ⟨_, window_code_lt hw _, (mem_initLang N x _ s).mpr rfl, _,
              window_code_lt hw _, (mem_edgeLang N x _ s).mpr ⟨_, hW.last, rfl, i, h1⟩,
              window_reach_of_rcode hw ((ExpBFS.rcode_iff s _).mpr ⟨_, hW, rfl⟩)⟩
        have hstep : wd.take (j + 1) = wd.take j ++ [wd[j]'(by omega)] :=
          (List.take_concat_get' wd j (by omega)).symm
        have hnext : Cfg.InWindow s (N.tm.runWith (wd.take j ++ [wd[j]'(by omega)])
            (N.tm.initCfg x)) := by
          rw [NDTM.runWith_append, NDTM.runWith_cons, NDTM.runWith_nil, stepWith_eq_apply]
          exact hW.last.apply_of_lt hlt le_rfl _
        rw [hstep]
        exact hW.snoc _ hnext
    have hW := key wd.length le_rfl
    rw [List.take_length] at hW
    exact ⟨_, window_code_lt hw _, (mem_initLang N x _ s).mpr rfl, _, window_code_lt hw _,
      (mem_acceptLang N x _ s).mpr ⟨_, hW.last, rfl, hhalt, hout⟩,
      window_reach_of_rcode hw ((ExpBFS.rcode_iff s _).mpr ⟨wd, hW, rfl⟩)⟩
  · rintro ⟨u, -, hinit, v, -, hacc, hr⟩
    exact mem_of_codePath h x s u v hinit (reflTransGen_of_reach _ _ w u v hr) hacc

end Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM
```

## ===== TCSlib/Complexity/TuringMachine/Build/CfgRecord.lean =====

```
/-

Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Seyoon Ragavan
-/
import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Bits
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.Catalog
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.SymbolLift
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.InputCall
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.Contract
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.CfgFacts

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Machine-construction library: configuration records over a rich alphabet (§12.8)

The record carrier of the §12.8 rich-alphabet design
(`machine-library-design.md` §12.8a §2, decision 12.8.1): a configuration of a
`Bool` machine with work tapes inside a radius-`s` window, written as a list of
fields over the rich alphabet `Turing.RecSym`. Records are what the
configuration-graph searches of chapter 4 (the reachability simulation of
`NSPACE` in `DSPACE` by breadth-first search, Savitch's midpoint recursion)
keep on their tapes, and the record rows are the machines that read, step and
compare them.

**Status.** Everything here is proved: the pure decoding facts and all three record rows.
The rows compose the framed catalog and counter rows through their contracts
(`Turing.Contract.segment` and each row's field equations) inside one phase host, and
join the phases by `Turing.Segment.trans`. No public result or private helper in this
module is admitted.

## Design

* **One cell per simulated cell.** A tape field holds the `2s + 1` window cells
  of one work tape, each a content track and a head-mark track
  (`Turing.RecSym.cell`). The input position is a fixed-width binary field of
  digits, `O(log n)` cells, and the state and the tag take one cell each. A
  record therefore has `k(2s + 1) + posWidth n + 2` cells and `k + 2`
  separators, which is `O(S n)` at radius `O(S n)` for `S ≥ log`.
* **Blank-separated fields** (`Turing.joinFields`): every field is a §12.6
  delimited word in place (`Turing.fieldsTape_field`), so the framed catalog
  rows apply field by field, and no field is empty, so two blanks end a table.
* **Digits are the lift's `e`.** `Turing.RecSym.digitEmb` is the embedding
  along which the `Bool` counter rows run on rich tapes
  (`Turing.MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols`), and the native input of a rich
  simulator is the input's image under it.
* **The window predicate** `Turing.Cfg.InWindow` lives here, relocated
  verbatim from `TCSlib.Complexity.ClassPSPACE.TQBF` (decision 12.8.2), which
  now imports it, so the record carrier and the adjacency codec share one
  definition.
* **Record rows are existential modules** in the `exists_installCallTM` style:
  a machine, entry and verdict anchors, and a linear first-return bound, with
  every head, the input position and the scratch restored.

## Main definitions

* `Turing.Cfg.InWindow` — the radius-`s` window predicate (relocated).
* `Turing.RecSym`, `Turing.RecSym.digitEmb` — the record alphabet and its
  digit embedding.
* `Turing.binDigits`, `Turing.posWidth` — fixed-width binary digits and the
  input-position width.
* `Turing.cfgRecord` — the record of a configuration.
* `Turing.RecordValid`, `Turing.RecordAt` — valid records, and a record laid
  out at a head.

## Main results

* `Turing.cfgRecord_length` — a record has `k + 3` fields.
* `Turing.Cfg.inWindow_init` — the initial configuration is in every window.
* `Turing.Cfg.InWindow.mono`, `Turing.Cfg.InWindow.apply_iff` — windows grow with the
  radius; one action keeps a window configuration in its window exactly when no head
  crosses a boundary.
* `Turing.Cfg.InWindow.apply_of_lt` — a step from a window configuration whose heads are
  strictly inside a radius stays in that radius's window.
* `Turing.cfgRecord_inj` — on windowed configurations, records agree exactly
  when configuration cores and tags do (proved; fill-C status update).
* `Turing.recordValid_iff` — validity as a field-by-field shape condition
  (proved; fill-C status update).
* `Turing.exists_recordStepTM`, `Turing.exists_recordEqTM`,
  `Turing.exists_recordTestTM` — the record rows R8.7: one simulated step, record
  equality, and a test of the state and tag (fill-C continuation 3 status update:
  all three are proved).
* `Turing.recordAt_iff`, `Turing.record_pos_lt` — reading a record and the position-width
  bound, the specification API (user, 2026-10-16).

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§4.1.1: the configuration graph and
  Claim 4.4(1), the `O(S(n))`-bit description of a configuration;
  Theorem 4.2(iii) and Theorem 4.14 (Savitch), whose simulations search the
  graph keeping configuration descriptions on work tapes. The record adds an
  `O(log n)` input-position field, as the book's description does.)
-/

namespace Turing

/-! ### The window predicate -/

/-- A configuration lies **in the radius-`s` window** when every work head
sits within `[-s, s]` and every work cell outside `[-s, s]` is blank — the
side condition under which the packaged codec of
`Complexity.exists_adjacency_codec_cnf` is faithful. (The input head needs no
clause: its type bounds it.) It is equally the side condition under which a
configuration record determines its configuration core, together with its
separately supplied tag (`Turing.cfgRecord_inj`);
relocated here from `TCSlib.Complexity.ClassPSPACE.TQBF` (decision 12.8.2). -/
def Cfg.InWindow {k : ℕ} {Symbol State : Type} {x : List Symbol} (s : ℕ)
    (c : Cfg k Symbol State x) : Prop :=
  (∀ i, |c.workTapePos i| ≤ (s : ℤ)) ∧
  ∀ (i : Fin k) (z : ℤ), (s : ℤ) < |z| → c.workTapes i z = none

/-- **Windows grow with the radius**: a configuration in the radius-`s` window is in the
radius-`s'` window whenever `s ≤ s'`. -/
theorem Cfg.InWindow.mono {k : ℕ} {Symbol State : Type} {x : List Symbol} {s s' : ℕ}
    {c : Cfg k Symbol State x} (hc : c.InWindow s) (hs : s ≤ s') : c.InWindow s' :=
  ⟨fun i => (hc.1 i).trans (by exact_mod_cast hs),
    fun i z hz => hc.2 i z (lt_of_le_of_lt (by exact_mod_cast hs) hz)⟩

/-- **One step from a window**: if `c` lies in the radius-`s` window, then applying an action `a`
keeps it there exactly when, for every work tape `i`, the head is not at `-s` with `a` moving it
left, and not at `s` with `a` moving it right. The write lands under the old head, which is inside
the window, so it cannot create a nonblank cell outside.

**Proof sketch.** Split the three possible moves. Interior positions stay inside; at each
boundary only its outward move fails. Outside cells are unchanged by the point update. -/
theorem Cfg.InWindow.apply_iff {k : ℕ} {Symbol State : Type} {x : List Symbol} {s : ℕ}
    {c : Cfg k Symbol State x} (hc : c.InWindow s) (a : Action k Symbol State) :
    (a.apply c).InWindow s ↔ ∀ i,
      ¬ (c.workTapePos i = -(s : ℤ) ∧ (a.workTapes i).2 = -1) ∧
      ¬ (c.workTapePos i = (s : ℤ) ∧ (a.workTapes i).2 = 1) := by
  have heads (i : Fin k) : |c.workTapePos i + ((a.workTapes i).2 : ℤ)| ≤ (s : ℤ) ↔
      ¬ (c.workTapePos i = -(s : ℤ) ∧ (a.workTapes i).2 = -1) ∧
      ¬ (c.workTapePos i = (s : ℤ) ∧ (a.workTapes i).2 = 1) := by
    have h := hc.1 i
    rw [abs_le] at h ⊢
    cases hm : (a.workTapes i).2 <;>
      simp only [SignType.zero_eq_zero, SignType.neg_eq_neg_one, SignType.pos_eq_one,
        SignType.coe_zero, SignType.coe_neg, SignType.coe_one, Int.reduceNeg, add_zero,
        le_add_neg_iff_add_le, neg_add_le_iff_le_add, add_neg_le_iff_le_add,
        SignType.neg_eq_self_iff, SignType.self_eq_neg_iff, reduceCtorEq, zero_ne_one, one_ne_zero,
        and_false, and_true, true_and, and_self, not_false_eq_true, iff_true] at * <;>
      omega
  constructor
  · intro h i
    have hi := h.1 i
    rw [Action.apply_workTapePos] at hi
    exact (heads i).mp hi
  · intro h
    refine ⟨fun i => ?_, ?_⟩
    · rw [Action.apply_workTapePos]
      exact (heads i).mpr (h i)
    intro i z hz
    have hne : z ≠ c.workTapePos i := by
      intro he
      subst z
      have := hc.1 i
      omega
    rw [Action.apply_workTapes, Function.update_of_ne hne]
    exact hc.2 i z hz

/-! ### The record alphabet -/

/-- **The record alphabet** (design §12.8a §2) over machine states `Q` and tags
`T`: binary digits, simulated work cells with a head-mark track, the state
cell, and the tag cell. Fields of a record are separated by blank cells. -/
inductive RecSym (Q T : Type) where
  /-- a binary digit: the input-position field, counters, and the native input -/
  | digit (b : Bool)
  /-- one simulated work cell: its content and whether the head is on it -/
  | cell (content : Option Bool) (mark : Bool)
  /-- the state cell, `none` for halted -/
  | st (q : Option Q)
  /-- the tag cell: a summary of what the run has emitted -/
  | tag (τ : T)
deriving DecidableEq

/-- The record alphabet is finite when the states and tags are; this is the
`Fintype` instance `Turing.FinTM.alphabet_reduction` needs. -/
instance recSymFintype (Q T : Type) [Fintype Q] [Fintype T] : Fintype (RecSym Q T) :=
  derive_fintype% _

/-- **The digit embedding** (design §12.8a §2): `Bool` into the record alphabet
by `Turing.RecSym.digit`. It is the `e` along which `Bool` rows and the `Bool`
input are lifted to rich tapes (`Turing.MultiTapeTM.liftSymbols`). -/
def RecSym.digitEmb (Q T : Type) : Bool ↪ RecSym Q T :=
  ⟨RecSym.digit, fun _ _ h => by cases h; rfl⟩

/-- The digit embedding sends a bit to its digit symbol: `RecSym.digitEmb Q T b = RecSym.digit b`
(the specification API, the briefs' pre-ship inventories, 2026-10-16). -/
theorem RecSym.digitEmb_apply (Q T : Type) (b : Bool) : RecSym.digitEmb Q T b = RecSym.digit b :=
  rfl

/-! ### The record -/

/-- **Fixed-width binary digits** (design §12.8a §2): the `w` low bits of `v`,
least significant first. -/
def binDigits (w v : ℕ) : List Bool := (List.range w).map v.testBit

/-- The `w` low bits of `v`, least significant first: `binDigits w v = (range w).map v.testBit` (the
specification API, the briefs' pre-ship inventories, 2026-10-16). -/
theorem binDigits_eq (w v : ℕ) : binDigits w v = (List.range w).map v.testBit :=
  rfl

/-- **The input-position width** (design §12.8a §2) at input length `n`: the
bit length of `n + 1`, so that `2 ^ posWidth n > n + 1` and every input
position `0, …, n + 1` has a distinct `Turing.binDigits` code. -/
def posWidth (n : ℕ) : ℕ := (Nat.bits (n + 1)).length

/-- The input-position width is the bit length of `n + 1`: `posWidth n = (Nat.bits (n + 1)).length`
(the specification API, the briefs' pre-ship inventories, 2026-10-16). -/
theorem posWidth_eq (n : ℕ) : posWidth n = (Nat.bits (n + 1)).length :=
  rfl

/-- **The configuration record** (design §12.8a §2) of `c` at window radius
`s` with tag `τ`: `k + 3` fields. Field `0` is the state, field `1` the input
position in `Turing.binDigits` of width `Turing.posWidth |x|`, fields `2` to
`k + 1` the window cells `-s, …, s` of each work tape with their head marks,
and field `k + 2` the tag. The output tape is not recorded; the tag summarizes
it. -/
def cfgRecord {k : ℕ} {Q T : Type} {x : List Bool} (s : ℕ) (c : Cfg k Bool Q x) (τ : T) :
    List (List (RecSym Q T)) :=
  [RecSym.st c.state] ::
    ((binDigits (posWidth x.length) c.inputPos.val).map RecSym.digit) ::
    (((List.finRange k).map fun i => (List.range (2 * s + 1)).map fun j =>
      RecSym.cell (c.workTapes i ((j : ℤ) - s)) (decide (c.workTapePos i = (j : ℤ) - s))) ++
    [[RecSym.tag τ]])

/-- **Record length** (design §12.8a §2): a record has `k + 3` fields, whatever
the configuration, radius and tag. -/
theorem cfgRecord_length {k : ℕ} {Q T : Type} {x : List Bool} (s : ℕ) (c : Cfg k Bool Q x)
    (τ : T) : (cfgRecord s c τ).length = k + 3 := by
  simp [cfgRecord]

/-- Every native input position is strictly below the power of two specified by its width:
`n + 2 ≤ 2 ^ posWidth n`. (Public since the specification API, user 2026-10-16.)

**Proof sketch.** `posWidth n` is the bit length of `n + 1`, which is its `Nat.size`. -/
theorem record_pos_lt (n : ℕ) : n + 1 < 2 ^ posWidth n := by
  unfold posWidth
  rw [Nat.size_eq_bits_len]
  exact Nat.lt_size_self _

/-- Decoding the fixed-width digits recovers any value below the width's power of two.

**Proof sketch.** Remove the low bit and divide the value by two. The induction hypothesis
decodes the remaining bits; the quotient-remainder identity restores the original value. -/
private theorem record_digits_value (w v : ℕ) (hv : v < 2 ^ w) :
    Nat.ofDigits 2 ((binDigits w v).map Bool.toNat) = v := by
  induction w generalizing v with
  | zero => simp at hv; subst hv; simp [binDigits]
  | succ w ih =>
    have hbits : binDigits (w + 1) v = v.testBit 0 :: binDigits w (v / 2) := by
      simp only [binDigits, List.range_succ_eq_map, List.map_cons, List.map_map]
      congr 1
      apply List.map_congr_left
      intro i _
      simp [Nat.testBit_add_one]
    rw [hbits, List.map_cons, Nat.ofDigits_cons, ih (v / 2) (by rw [pow_succ] at hv; omega)]
    rw [Nat.testBit_zero]
    rcases Nat.mod_two_eq_zero_or_one v with h | h <;> simp [h] <;> omega

/-- Fixed-width digit strings distinguish the values in their representable range. -/
private theorem record_digits_inj (w u v : ℕ) (hu : u < 2 ^ w) (hv : v < 2 ^ w)
    (h : binDigits w u = binDigits w v) : u = v := by
  rw [← record_digits_value w u hu, ← record_digits_value w v hv, h]

/-- **Canonical decoding** (design §12.8a §2). On windowed configurations of
one input, records agree exactly when the configurations agree on state, input
position, work tapes and work heads, and the tags agree. The output is not
compared, so this is injectivity on the configuration core, the vertex
quotient of the configuration graph.

**Proof sketch.** Compare the fields. The state field gives the state. The
position field is `Turing.binDigits` at a width with `2 ^ posWidth |x| >
|x| + 1`, which is injective on values `≤ |x| + 1`, the range of input
positions. For tape `i`, the content track gives the cells in `[-s, s]`, and
outside it both configurations are blank by the window hypothesis. The mark
track has exactly one mark, at the head, which lies in `[-s, s]`. The tag field
gives the tag. -/
theorem cfgRecord_inj {k : ℕ} {Q T : Type} {x : List Bool} (s : ℕ) {c d : Cfg k Bool Q x}
    {τ τ' : T} (hc : c.InWindow s) (hd : d.InWindow s) :
    cfgRecord s c τ = cfgRecord s d τ' ↔
      (c.state = d.state ∧ c.inputPos = d.inputPos ∧ c.workTapes = d.workTapes ∧
        c.workTapePos = d.workTapePos) ∧ τ = τ' := by
  classical
  constructor
  · intro h
    simp only [cfgRecord, List.cons.injEq, bind_pure_comp, Functor.map, List.map_map, Function.comp_def] at h
    obtain ⟨hstate, hpos, hrest⟩ := h
    have hs : c.state = d.state := by simpa using hstate
    have hb : binDigits (posWidth x.length) c.inputPos.val =
        binDigits (posWidth x.length) d.inputPos.val :=
      (List.map_inj_right (fun _ _ h => RecSym.digit.inj h)).mp hpos
    have hp : c.inputPos = d.inputPos := Fin.ext
      (record_digits_inj _ _ _
        (lt_of_le_of_lt (by have := c.inputPos.isLt; omega) (record_pos_lt x.length))
        (lt_of_le_of_lt (by have := d.inputPos.isLt; omega) (record_pos_lt x.length)) hb)
    obtain ⟨hfields, htag⟩ := List.append_inj' hrest (by rfl)
    have ht : τ = τ' := by simpa using htag
    have hcell (i : Fin k) (j : ℕ) (hj : j < 2 * s + 1) :
        RecSym.cell (Q := Q) (T := T) (c.workTapes i ((j : ℤ) - s))
            (decide (c.workTapePos i = (j : ℤ) - s)) =
          RecSym.cell (d.workTapes i ((j : ℤ) - s))
            (decide (d.workTapePos i = (j : ℤ) - s)) := by
      have hi := List.map_inj_left.mp hfields i (by simp)
      exact List.map_inj_left.mp hi j (List.mem_range.mpr hj)
    have hw : c.workTapes = d.workTapes := by
      funext i z
      by_cases hz : |z| ≤ (s : ℤ)
      · have hz' := abs_le.mp hz
        have hnat : (((z + s).toNat : ℕ) : ℤ) = z + s := Int.toNat_of_nonneg (by omega)
        have h := (RecSym.cell.inj (hcell i (z + s).toNat (by omega))).1
        simpa only [hnat, add_sub_cancel_right] using h
      · rw [hc.2 i z (by omega), hd.2 i z (by omega)]
    have hh : c.workTapePos = d.workTapePos := by
      funext i
      have hi := abs_le.mp (hc.1 i)
      have hnat : (((c.workTapePos i + s).toNat : ℕ) : ℤ) = c.workTapePos i + s :=
        Int.toNat_of_nonneg (by omega)
      have h := (RecSym.cell.inj (hcell i (c.workTapePos i + s).toNat (by omega))).2
      simp only [hnat, add_sub_cancel_right, decide_true] at h
      exact (of_decide_eq_true h.symm).symm
    exact ⟨⟨hs, hp, hw, hh⟩, ht⟩
  · rintro ⟨⟨hs, hp, hw, hh⟩, ht⟩
    simp only [cfgRecord, hs, hp, hw, hh, ht]

/-- **Valid records** (design §12.8a §2): the field list is the record, at
radius `s`, of some windowed configuration on some input of length `n`, with
some tag. -/
def RecordValid (k n s : ℕ) (Q T : Type) (fs : List (List (RecSym Q T))) : Prop :=
  ∃ (x : List Bool) (c : Cfg k Bool Q x) (τ : T), x.length = n ∧ c.InWindow s ∧
    cfgRecord s c τ = fs

/-- **Validity is a shape condition** (design §12.8a §2). A field list is a
valid record exactly when it has `k + 3` fields: a state cell; `posWidth n`
digits of a value at most `n + 1`; for each tape, `2s + 1` work cells of which
exactly one carries the head mark; and a tag cell. This shape supports a
validity machine built from finite-state folds over the fields, given the
widths `2s + 1` and `posWidth n` and the bound `n + 1` as templates or
counters. A fold of one field alone cannot check a variable width: a single
marked cell is valid at `s = 0` and not at `s = 1`. The validator itself is
deferred to S1b's statement phase.

**Proof sketch.** Forward: read the shape off `Turing.cfgRecord`, with the mark
at index `pos + s` of each tape field, which is in range by the window
hypothesis. Backward: take the input `List.replicate n false`, the state and
the tag from their cells, the input position from the digits, and for tape `i`
the cell at `z` from index `z + s` of its field when `|z| ≤ s`, and blank
otherwise, with the head at the mark minus `s`. This configuration is windowed
and its record is the given list. -/
theorem recordValid_iff {k : ℕ} {Q T : Type} (n s : ℕ) (fs : List (List (RecSym Q T))) :
    RecordValid k n s Q T fs ↔
      fs.length = k + 3 ∧
      (∃ q : Option Q, fs[0]? = some [RecSym.st q]) ∧
      (∃ v ≤ n + 1, fs[1]? = some ((binDigits (posWidth n) v).map RecSym.digit)) ∧
      (∀ i : Fin k, ∃ (cs : ℕ → Option Bool) (m : ℕ), m < 2 * s + 1 ∧
        fs[i.val + 2]? = some ((List.range (2 * s + 1)).map fun j =>
          RecSym.cell (cs j) (decide (j = m)))) ∧
      (∃ τ : T, fs[k + 2]? = some [RecSym.tag τ]) := by
  classical
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨x, c, τ, rfl, hc, rfl⟩
    refine ⟨cfgRecord_length s c τ, ⟨c.state, rfl⟩,
      ⟨c.inputPos.val, by have := c.inputPos.isLt; omega, rfl⟩, ?_, ⟨τ, ?_⟩⟩
    · intro i
      have hi := abs_le.mp (hc.1 i)
      have hnat : (((c.workTapePos i + s).toNat : ℕ) : ℤ) = c.workTapePos i + s :=
        Int.toNat_of_nonneg (by omega)
      refine ⟨fun j => c.workTapes i ((j : ℤ) - s), (c.workTapePos i + s).toNat,
        by omega, ?_⟩
      simp only [cfgRecord, List.getElem?_cons_succ, bind_pure_comp, Functor.map, List.map_map, Function.comp_def]
      rw [List.getElem?_append_left (by simp), List.getElem?_map,
        List.getElem?_eq_getElem (by simp)]
      simp only [List.getElem_finRange, Option.map_some, Option.some.injEq]
      apply List.map_congr_left
      intro j _
      congr 1
      rw [decide_eq_decide]
      change (c.workTapePos i = (j : ℤ) - s) ↔ j = (c.workTapePos i + s).toNat
      omega
    · simp [cfgRecord, List.length_finRange]
  · rintro ⟨hlen, ⟨q, hq⟩, ⟨v, hv, hpos⟩, htapes, ⟨τ, htag⟩⟩
    choose cs m hm hfield using htapes
    let c : Cfg k Bool Q (List.replicate n false) :=
      ⟨q, ⟨v, by simpa using (show v < n + 2 by omega)⟩,
        (fun i z => if |z| ≤ (s : ℤ) then cs i (z + s).toNat else none),
        (fun i => (m i : ℤ) - s), []⟩
    have hc : c.InWindow s := by
      constructor
      · intro i
        change |(m i : ℤ) - s| ≤ (s : ℤ)
        have := hm i
        rw [abs_le]
        omega
      · intro i z hz
        change (if |z| ≤ (s : ℤ) then _ else _) = none
        rw [if_neg (by omega)]
    refine ⟨List.replicate n false, c, τ, List.length_replicate .., hc, ?_⟩
    apply List.ext_getElem?
    intro j
    by_cases hj : j < k + 3
    · rcases j with _ | (_ | j)
      · exact hq.symm
      · simpa [cfgRecord, c] using hpos.symm
      · by_cases hlast : j = k
        · subst j
          simpa [cfgRecord, c, List.getElem?_append] using htag.symm
        · have hjk : j < k := by omega
          let i : Fin k := ⟨j, hjk⟩
          rw [hfield i]
          simp only [cfgRecord, List.getElem?_cons_succ, bind_pure_comp, Functor.map, List.map_map, Function.comp_def]
          rw [List.getElem?_append_left (by simpa using hjk), List.getElem?_map,
            List.getElem?_eq_getElem (by simpa using hjk)]
          simp only [List.getElem_finRange, Option.map_some, Option.some.injEq]
          apply List.map_congr_left
          intro a ha
          have ha' := List.mem_range.mp ha
          have hz : |(a : ℤ) - s| ≤ (s : ℤ) := by rw [abs_le]; omega
          simp only [c, hz, if_pos, sub_add_cancel, Int.toNat_natCast]
          congr 1
          rw [decide_eq_decide]
          change ((m i : ℤ) - s = (a : ℤ) - s) ↔ a = m i
          omega
    · rw [List.getElem?_eq_none (by rw [cfgRecord_length]; omega),
        List.getElem?_eq_none (by omega)]

/-- **A record at a head** (design §12.8a §2): tape `r` holds the field layout
of `fs` from its head, delimited by blanks at relative positions `-1` and
`|joinFields fs|`. The cells beyond the delimiters are arbitrary. -/
def RecordAt {K : ℕ} {Γ S : Type*} {x : List Γ} (d : Cfg K Γ S x) (r : Fin K)
    (fs : List (List Γ)) : Prop :=
  ∀ p : ℤ, -1 ≤ p → p ≤ ((joinFields fs).length : ℤ) →
    d.workTapes r (d.workTapePos r + p) = fieldsTape fs p

/-- **Reading a record** (the specification API, user 2026-10-16): `RecordAt d r fs` holds
exactly when, at every offset `p` with `-1 ≤ p ≤ |joinFields fs|`, the cell of tape `r` at its
head plus `p` holds `fieldsTape fs p`: the layout's cells, with blank delimiters at offsets `-1`
and `|joinFields fs|`. Cells outside that interval are unconstrained. -/
theorem recordAt_iff {K : ℕ} {Γ S : Type*} {x : List Γ} (d : Cfg K Γ S x) (r : Fin K)
    (fs : List (List Γ)) :
    RecordAt d r fs ↔ ∀ p : ℤ, -1 ≤ p → p ≤ ((joinFields fs).length : ℤ) →
      d.workTapes r (d.workTapePos r + p) = fieldsTape fs p :=
  Iff.rfl

/-! ### R8.7 — the record rows -/

/-- The shared segment specialized to the record verdicts and the common head box. -/
private abbrev RecordSeg {K : ℕ} {Γ S : Type} {x : List Γ} (R : MultiTapeTM K Γ S)
    (yes no : S) (base : Fin K → ℤ) (radius : ℕ) (a b : Cfg K Γ S x) (t : ℕ) : Prop :=
  Segment R {some yes, some no}
    (HeadBox (fun j => base j - radius) (fun j => base j + radius)) a b t

/-- The record's radius condition is the shared interval box, read through its API. -/
private theorem record_headBox_iff {K : ℕ} (base : Fin K → ℤ) (radius : ℕ)
    (p : Fin K → ℤ) :
    HeadBox (fun j => base j - radius) (fun j => base j + radius) p ↔
      ∀ j, |p j - base j| ≤ (radius : ℤ) := by
  rw [headBox_iff]
  apply forall_congr'
  intro j
  rw [Finset.mem_Icc, abs_le]
  omega

/-- Reading a record segment in the radius form required by the frozen public rows.
This is only the shared segment's characterization and the box/radius equivalence. -/
private theorem recordSeg_iff {K : ℕ} {Γ S : Type} {x : List Γ}
    {R : MultiTapeTM K Γ S} {yes no : S} {base : Fin K → ℤ} {radius : ℕ}
    {a b : Cfg K Γ S x} {t : ℕ} :
    RecordSeg R yes no base radius a b t ↔
      R.runFrom a t = b ∧
        (∀ u < t, (R.runFrom a u).state ≠ some yes ∧ (R.runFrom a u).state ≠ some no) ∧
