Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Hydroxyi
-/
import TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.ConfigGraph
import TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Machines.Parse

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# A configuration codec for nondeterministic machines

Configuration-graph algorithms in small space — Savitch's midpoint recursion, the `PATH`
reduction, the inductive counting of Immerman and Szelepcsényi [AB09, §4.1.1, §4.2, §4.3]
— store configurations of a fixed machine `N` on the real input `x` as numbers in
registers. This file fixes that representation: the **code** of a configuration whose work
heads and nonblank work cells lie in the window `[-s, s]` is a word of `O(s + log |x|)` bits,
read as a little-endian number.

## Layout

The code word `Complexity.Codec.cfgWord N s C` is

* `2s + 1` **chunks**, one per work-tape cell `z ∈ [-s, s]` in increasing order, each of the
  fixed width `Complexity.Codec.W N`: a one-hot *header slot* (nonzero only in the leftmost
  chunk, where it names the control state and the output summary), then three bits per work
  tape (`nonblank`, `symbol`, `head here`), then a constant `1`;
* the input head position in binary, little-endian, padded to the fixed width
  `|bits (|x| + 1)|`;
* a final `1`, so that the word is the binary word of its value.

Fixed widths make field extraction position arithmetic, and the cell-major order makes one
machine step a *local* relation between neighbouring chunks (the checks of
`TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.Codec.Checks`). The code records exactly the
configuration-graph vertex `Turing.NDTM.coreSum` (state, input position, windowed work tapes,
work heads, output summary), so it is injective on window-bounded configurations up to that
vertex, and that is all the graph algorithms need.

This codec is configuration-graph infrastructure, not a result of [AB09]; its conventions
(the window `Turing.Cfg.InWindow` of radius `s`, the output summary) are those of
`TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.ConfigGraph`.

## Main definitions

* `Complexity.Codec.CellV`, `Complexity.Codec.encChunk` — cell values and their chunks.
* `Complexity.Codec.cfgWord`, `Complexity.Codec.cfgCode` — the code word and the code.
* `Complexity.Codec.decodeCfg` — the decoder.

## Main results

* `Complexity.Codec.bits_cfgCode` — the binary word of the code is the code word.
* `Complexity.Codec.cfgWord_congr` — the code depends only on the vertex `coreSum`.
* `Complexity.Codec.coreSum_eq_of_cfgWord_eq` — on window-bounded configurations the code
  determines the vertex.
* `Complexity.Codec.length_cfgWord`, `Complexity.Codec.cfgCode_lt` — the code has at most
  `codeK N · (s + logSpace |x| + 1)` bits.
* `Complexity.Codec.decodeCfg_cfgCode` — decoding a code recovers the vertex.

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§4.1.1: configurations and configuration graphs.)
-/

namespace Complexity.Codec

open Turing LogProg

variable (N : FinNDTM Bool)

/-! ## Words -/

/-- The index of an output summary. -/
def sumIdx : OutSummary → Fin 3
  | .empty => 0
  | .accept => 1
  | .dead => 2

/-- Distinct summaries have distinct indices. -/
lemma sumIdx_injective : Function.Injective sumIdx := by
  intro a b h; cases a <;> cases b <;> simp_all [sumIdx]

/-- The header datum of a configuration: its control state and output-summary index. -/
abbrev Hd := Option N.State × Fin 3

/-- A cell value: the header (present only in the leftmost cell) and, per work tape, the
symbol in the cell and whether the head is on it. -/
abbrev CellV := Option (Hd N) × (Fin N.k → Option Bool × Bool)

set_option synthInstance.maxSize 1000 in
/-- Cell values have decidable equality. -/
instance CellV.instDecidableEq : DecidableEq (CellV N) := inferInstance

/-- The width of the header slot: the number of header data. -/
def hH : ℕ := Fintype.card (Hd N)

/-- The width of a chunk: header slot, three bits per work tape, a final `1`. -/
def W : ℕ := hH N + 3 * N.k + 1

/-- The chunk width: the header slot, three bits per work tape, and the closing `1`. -/
lemma W_eq : W N = hH N + 3 * N.k + 1 := rfl

/-- The position of a header datum in the one-hot header slot. -/
noncomputable def hdNum (h : Hd N) : ℕ := (Fintype.equivFin (Hd N) h).val

/-- Header positions lie in the slot. -/
lemma hdNum_lt (h : Hd N) : hdNum N h < hH N := (Fintype.equivFin (Hd N) h).isLt

/-- Distinct header data have distinct positions. -/
lemma hdNum_injective : Function.Injective (hdNum N) := by
  intro a b h
  exact (Fintype.equivFin (Hd N)).injective (Fin.ext h)

/-- Bit `t` of the chunk of a cell value: the one-hot header slot, then per tape `nonblank`,
`symbol`, `head here`, then `1`. -/
noncomputable def chunkBit (cv : CellV N) (t : ℕ) : Bool :=
  if t < hH N then decide (cv.1.map (hdNum N) = some t)
  else if h : (t - hH N) / 3 < N.k then
    if (t - hH N) % 3 = 0 then (cv.2 ⟨(t - hH N) / 3, h⟩).1.isSome
    else if (t - hH N) % 3 = 1 then (cv.2 ⟨(t - hH N) / 3, h⟩).1.getD false
    else (cv.2 ⟨(t - hH N) / 3, h⟩).2
  else true

/-- The chunk of a cell value. -/
noncomputable def encChunk (cv : CellV N) : List Bool :=
  List.ofFn fun t : Fin (W N) => chunkBit N cv t

/-- Chunks have the fixed width `W N`. -/
@[simp] lemma length_encChunk (cv : CellV N) : (encChunk N cv).length = W N := by
  simp only [encChunk, List.length_ofFn]

/-- Bits of a chunk below its width are `chunkBit`. -/
lemma getD_encChunk (cv : CellV N) (t : ℕ) (ht : t < W N) :
    (encChunk N cv).getD t false = chunkBit N cv t := by
  simp only [encChunk, List.getD_eq_getElem?_getD, List.getElem?_ofFn, ht, dite_true,
    Option.getD_some]

/-- The header-slot bits of a chunk. -/
lemma chunkBit_slot (cv : CellV N) (t : ℕ) (ht : t < hH N) :
    chunkBit N cv t = decide (cv.1.map (hdNum N) = some t) := by
  simp [chunkBit, ht]

/-- The three bits of tape `i` in a chunk. -/
lemma chunkBit_tape (cv : CellV N) (i : Fin N.k) (r : ℕ) (hr : r < 3) :
    chunkBit N cv (hH N + 3 * i + r) =
      if r = 0 then (cv.2 i).1.isSome else if r = 1 then (cv.2 i).1.getD false
      else (cv.2 i).2 := by
  have e1 : (hH N + 3 * i + r - hH N) / 3 = i := by omega
  have e2 : (hH N + 3 * i + r - hH N) % 3 = r := by omega
  have hi : (hH N + 3 * i + r - hH N) / 3 < N.k := by rw [e1]; exact i.isLt
  simp only [chunkBit, show ¬ hH N + 3 * i + r < hH N by omega, ↓reduceIte, dif_pos hi, e2]
  have : (⟨(hH N + 3 * i + r - hH N) / 3, hi⟩ : Fin N.k) = i := Fin.ext e1
  rw [this]

/-- **Chunks are injective**: a cell value is determined by its chunk.

**Proof sketch.** Compare the chunks bit by bit (`getD_encChunk`): the one-hot header slot
determines the header (positions are injective, `hdNum_injective`), and the three bits of each
tape determine the optional symbol and the head flag (`chunkBit_tape`). -/
theorem encChunk_injective : Function.Injective (encChunk N) := by
  intro a b h
  have hb : ∀ t < W N, chunkBit N a t = chunkBit N b t := by
    intro t ht
    rw [← getD_encChunk N a t ht, ← getD_encChunk N b t ht, h]
  obtain ⟨a1, a2⟩ := a
  obtain ⟨b1, b2⟩ := b
  have slot : a1 = b1 := by
    have key : ∀ (u v : Option (Hd N)), (∀ t < hH N, decide (u.map (hdNum N) = some t) =
        decide (v.map (hdNum N) = some t)) → ∀ h, u = some h → v = some h := by
      intro u v hu h hh
      have := hu (hdNum N h) (hdNum_lt N h)
      subst hh
      simp only [Option.map_some, decide_true] at this
      cases v with
      | none => simp at this
      | some g =>
        simp at this
        rw [hdNum_injective N this]
    have hs : ∀ t < hH N, decide (a1.map (hdNum N) = some t) =
        decide (b1.map (hdNum N) = some t) := by
      intro t ht
      have := hb t (by simp only [W]; omega)
      rwa [chunkBit_slot N _ t ht, chunkBit_slot N _ t ht] at this
    cases a1 with
    | some hd => exact (key _ _ hs hd rfl).symm
    | none =>
      cases b1 with
      | none => rfl
      | some g => exact absurd (key _ _ (fun t ht => (hs t ht).symm) g rfl) (by simp)
  subst slot
  congr 1
  funext i
  have bit (r : ℕ) (hr : r < 3) := hb (hH N + 3 * i + r) (by simp only [W]; omega)
  have e0 := bit 0 (by omega)
  have e1 := bit 1 (by omega)
  have e2 := bit 2 (by omega)
  simp only [chunkBit_tape N _ i _ (by omega : (0 : ℕ) < 3),
    chunkBit_tape N _ i _ (by omega : (1 : ℕ) < 3),
    chunkBit_tape N _ i _ (by omega : (2 : ℕ) < 3)] at e0 e1 e2
  simp only [↓reduceIte, one_ne_zero, OfNat.ofNat_ne_zero, OfNat.ofNat_ne_one] at e0 e1 e2
  revert e0 e1 e2
  obtain ⟨o, hh⟩ := a2 i
  obtain ⟨o', hh'⟩ := b2 i
  intro e0 e1 e2
  simp only at e0 e1 e2
  subst e2
  congr 1
  cases o <;> cases o' <;> simp_all

/-- Concatenated fixed-width blocks: block `j` is recovered by dropping `W · j` letters and
taking `W`. -/
lemma take_drop_flatten {α : Type} (L : List (List α)) (w : ℕ)
    (hL : ∀ b ∈ L, b.length = w) (j : ℕ) (hj : j < L.length) :
    ((L.flatten).drop (w * j)).take w = L[j] := by
  induction L generalizing j with
  | nil => simp at hj
  | cons b L ih =>
    have hb := hL b (by simp)
    cases j with
    | zero => simp [← hb]
    | succ j =>
      simp only [List.flatten_cons, List.getElem_cons_succ]
      rw [show w * (j + 1) = b.length + w * j by rw [hb]; ring, ← List.drop_drop,
        List.drop_left]
      exact ih (fun c hc => hL c (by simp [hc])) j (by simpa using hj)

/-- Concatenated blocks of width `w` have length `w` times their number. -/
lemma length_flatten_const {α : Type} (L : List (List α)) (w : ℕ)
    (hL : ∀ b ∈ L, b.length = w) : (L.flatten).length = w * L.length := by
  induction L with
  | nil => simp
  | cons b L ih =>
    simp only [List.flatten_cons, List.length_append, List.length_cons,
      hL b (by simp), ih (fun c hc => hL c (by simp [hc]))]
    ring

/-- The word of `m` chunks with cell values `f 0, …, f (m - 1)`. -/
noncomputable def chunksWord (f : ℕ → CellV N) (m : ℕ) : List Bool :=
  (List.ofFn fun j : Fin m => encChunk N (f j)).flatten

/-- A chunk word has `W N` letters per chunk. -/
lemma length_chunksWord (f : ℕ → CellV N) (m : ℕ) :
    (chunksWord N f m).length = W N * m := by
  rw [chunksWord, length_flatten_const _ (W N) (by simp)]
  simp

/-- Equal chunk words have equal cell values. -/
lemma chunksWord_inj {f g : ℕ → CellV N} {m : ℕ} (h : chunksWord N f m = chunksWord N g m)
    (j : ℕ) (hj : j < m) : f j = g j := by
  have e1 := take_drop_flatten (List.ofFn fun j : Fin m => encChunk N (f j)) (W N)
    (by simp) j (by simpa using hj)
  have e2 := take_drop_flatten (List.ofFn fun j : Fin m => encChunk N (g j)) (W N)
    (by simp) j (by simpa using hj)
  have e : (List.ofFn fun j : Fin m => encChunk N (f j))[j]'(by simpa using hj) =
      (List.ofFn fun j : Fin m => encChunk N (g j))[j]'(by simpa using hj) := by
    rw [← e1, ← e2]
    exact congrArg (fun w => (w.drop (W N * j)).take (W N)) h
  simp only [List.getElem_ofFn] at e
  exact encChunk_injective N e

/-! ## The code of a configuration -/

variable {N} {x : List Bool}

/-- The cell value of cell `j` (work position `j - s`) of a configuration: the header in the
leftmost cell, then per tape the symbol at `j - s` and whether the head is there. -/
def cellOf (s : ℕ) (C : Cfg N.k Bool N.State x) (j : ℕ) : CellV N :=
  (if j = 0 then some (C.state, sumIdx (outSummary C.output)) else none,
    fun i => (C.workTapes i ((j : ℤ) - s), decide (C.workTapePos i = (j : ℤ) - s)))

/-- The head flag of tape `i` in cell `j`: whether the head of tape `i` is at work position
`j - s`. -/
lemma cellOf_head (s : ℕ) (C : Cfg N.k Bool N.State x) (j : ℕ) (i : Fin N.k) :
    ((cellOf s C j).2 i).2 = decide (C.workTapePos i = (j : ℤ) - s) := rfl

/-- The width of the input-position field on inputs of length `n`: `|bits (n + 1)|`. -/
def wP (n : ℕ) : ℕ := (Nat.bits (n + 1)).length

/-- The position-field width is the binary length of `n + 1`. -/
lemma wP_eq (n : ℕ) : wP n = (Nat.bits (n + 1)).length := rfl

/-- The binary word of `v` padded with `0`s to width `w`. -/
def padBits (w v : ℕ) : List Bool := Nat.bits v ++ List.replicate (w - (Nat.bits v).length) false

/-- **The code word** of a configuration at window radius `s`: the `2s + 1` cell chunks, the
padded input position, and a final `1`. -/
noncomputable def cfgWord (s : ℕ) (C : Cfg N.k Bool N.State x) : List Bool :=
  chunksWord N (cellOf s C) (2 * s + 1) ++ padBits (wP x.length) C.inputPos.val ++ [true]

/-- **The code** of a configuration at window radius `s`: the value of its code word. -/
noncomputable def cfgCode (s : ℕ) (C : Cfg N.k Bool N.State x) : ℕ := bitsVal (cfgWord s C)

/-- The value of a word does not see trailing `0`s. -/
lemma bitsVal_append_replicate (w : List Bool) (z : ℕ) :
    bitsVal (w ++ List.replicate z false) = bitsVal w := by
  induction w with
  | nil =>
    induction z with
    | zero => rfl
    | succ z ih => simp [List.replicate_succ, bitsVal] at ih ⊢; exact ih
  | cons b w ih => simp [bitsVal, ih]

/-- Every word is the binary word of its value followed by `0`s.

**Proof sketch.** Induction on the word: a leading letter `b` contributes `b + 2 v`; the
binary word of that value is `b` followed by that of `v`, unless both vanish, when the word
is all `0`s. -/
lemma eq_bits_append_replicate (w : List Bool) :
    w = Nat.bits (bitsVal w) ++
      List.replicate (w.length - (Nat.bits (bitsVal w)).length) false := by
  induction w with
  | nil => simp [bitsVal, Nat.zero_bits]
  | cons b w ih =>
    have hl : (Nat.bits (bitsVal w)).length ≤ w.length := by
      have := congrArg List.length ih
      simp only [List.length_append, List.length_replicate] at this
      omega
    simp only [bitsVal, List.length_cons]
    rw [show b.toNat + 2 * bitsVal w = 2 * bitsVal w + b.toNat by ring]
    by_cases hz : bitsVal w = 0 ∧ b = false
    · obtain ⟨h0, rfl⟩ := hz
      rw [h0] at ih ⊢
      simp only [Nat.zero_bits, List.length_nil, Nat.sub_zero, List.nil_append] at ih ⊢
      simp only [Bool.toNat_false, Nat.mul_zero, Nat.add_zero, Nat.zero_bits, List.length_nil,
        Nat.sub_zero, List.nil_append, List.replicate_succ]
      rw [← ih]
    · rw [bits_two_mul_add _ _ (fun h0 => by
          cases b
          · exact absurd ⟨h0, rfl⟩ hz
          · rfl)]
      simp only [List.length_cons, List.cons_append, List.cons.injEq, true_and]
      rw [show w.length + 1 - ((Nat.bits (bitsVal w)).length + 1) =
        w.length - (Nat.bits (bitsVal w)).length by omega]
      exact ih

/-- A padded word has the padding width when the value fits. -/
lemma length_padBits {w v : ℕ} (h : (Nat.bits v).length ≤ w) : (padBits w v).length = w := by
  simp [padBits]; omega

/-- The value of a padded word. -/
@[simp] lemma bitsVal_padBits (w v : ℕ) : bitsVal (padBits w v) = v := by
  rw [padBits, bitsVal_append_replicate, bitsVal_bits]

/-- A word of length `w` is the padding of its value to width `w`. -/
lemma eq_padBits (p : List Bool) : p = padBits p.length (bitsVal p) := by
  conv_lhs => rw [eq_bits_append_replicate p]
  rfl

/-- Input positions fit their field. -/
lemma length_bits_pos_le (v n : ℕ) (hv : v ≤ n + 1) : (Nat.bits v).length ≤ wP n :=
  length_bits_mono hv

/-- The number of letters of the code word. -/
lemma length_cfgWord (s : ℕ) (C : Cfg N.k Bool N.State x) :
    (cfgWord s C).length = W N * (2 * s + 1) + wP x.length + 1 := by
  have := C.inputPos.isLt
  simp only [cfgWord, List.length_append, length_chunksWord, List.length_singleton]
  rw [length_padBits (length_bits_pos_le _ _ (by omega))]

/-- The code word ends with `1`, so it is the binary word of its value. -/
lemma canon_cfgWord (s : ℕ) (C : Cfg N.k Bool N.State x) : Canon (cfgWord s C) := by
  intro h
  simp [cfgWord]

/-- **The binary word of the code is the code word.** -/
theorem bits_cfgCode (s : ℕ) (C : Cfg N.k Bool N.State x) :
    Nat.bits (cfgCode s C) = cfgWord s C :=
  (canon_eq_bits _ (canon_cfgWord s C)).symm

/-- The cell values depend only on the configuration-graph vertex. -/
lemma cellOf_congr {s : ℕ} {C D : Cfg N.k Bool N.State x} (h : NDTM.coreSum C = NDTM.coreSum D) :
    cellOf s C = cellOf s D := by
  simp only [NDTM.coreSum, MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.core, Prod.mk.injEq] at h
  obtain ⟨⟨hs, -, hw, hp⟩, ho⟩ := h
  funext j
  simp only [cellOf, hs, hw, hp, ho]

/-- **The code depends only on the configuration-graph vertex** `coreSum`. -/
theorem cfgWord_congr {s : ℕ} {C D : Cfg N.k Bool N.State x}
    (h : NDTM.coreSum C = NDTM.coreSum D) : cfgWord s C = cfgWord s D := by
  have hi : C.inputPos = D.inputPos := by
    simp only [NDTM.coreSum, MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.core, Prod.mk.injEq] at h
    exact h.1.2.1
  simp only [cfgWord, cellOf_congr h, hi]

/-- **On window-bounded configurations the code determines the vertex**: equal code words
give equal `coreSum`.

**Proof sketch.** The two words have the same length, so their chunk prefixes, position
fields and final letters align. Equal chunks give equal cell values (`chunksWord_inj`):
the leftmost cell yields the state and the summary (`sumIdx` is injective, and summaries
determine the vertex component), every cell yields the tape symbols and head flags at its
position, and outside `[-s, s]` both tapes are blank and no head lies there (window
hypotheses). Equal position fields have equal values (`bitsVal_padBits`). -/
theorem coreSum_eq_of_cfgWord_eq {s : ℕ} {C D : Cfg N.k Bool N.State x}
    (hC : Cfg.InWindow s C) (hD : Cfg.InWindow s D) (h : cfgWord s C = cfgWord s D) :
    NDTM.coreSum C = NDTM.coreSum D := by
  have hlen : (chunksWord N (cellOf s C) (2 * s + 1)).length =
      (chunksWord N (cellOf s D) (2 * s + 1)).length := by simp [length_chunksWord]
  simp only [cfgWord, List.append_assoc] at h
  obtain ⟨hc, hrest⟩ := List.append_inj h hlen
  have hpos := congrArg bitsVal (List.append_inj_left' hrest rfl)
  simp only [bitsVal_padBits] at hpos
  have cell := chunksWord_inj N hc
  have c0 := cell 0 (by omega)
  simp only [cellOf, ↓reduceIte, Prod.mk.injEq, Option.some.injEq] at c0
  obtain ⟨⟨hst, hsum⟩, -⟩ := c0
  have hsum' := sumIdx_injective hsum
  have tape : ∀ i (z : ℤ), |z| ≤ s → C.workTapes i z = D.workTapes i z ∧
      (C.workTapePos i = z ↔ D.workTapePos i = z) := by
    intro i z hz
    have := cell (z + s).toNat (by rw [abs_le] at hz; omega)
    simp only [cellOf, Prod.mk.injEq] at this
    have e := congrFun this.2 i
    simp only [Prod.mk.injEq, decide_eq_decide] at e
    have hz' : (((z + s).toNat : ℕ) : ℤ) - s = z := by rw [abs_le] at hz; omega
    rwa [hz'] at e
  simp only [NDTM.coreSum, MultiTapeTM.ConfigCount.core, Prod.mk.injEq]
  refine ⟨⟨hst, Fin.ext hpos, ?_, ?_⟩, hsum'⟩
  · funext i z
    by_cases hz : |z| ≤ s
    · exact (tape i z hz).1
    · have h1 : C.workTapes i z = none := hC.2 i z (not_le.mp hz)
      have h2 : D.workTapes i z = none := hD.2 i z (not_le.mp hz)
      rw [h1, h2]
  · funext i
    exact ((tape i _ (hC.1 i)).2.mp rfl).symm

/-- The constant of the code length: `2 W + 2`. -/
def codeK (N : FinNDTM Bool) : ℕ := 2 * W N + 2

/-- **The code is short**: the code word has at most `codeK N · (s + logSpace |x| + 1)`
letters, so the code is below `2 ^ (codeK N · (s + logSpace |x| + 1))`. The input field
has `|bits (|x| + 1)| ≤ logSpace |x| + 1` letters.

**Proof sketch.** Count `W (2s + 1)` chunk letters, the position field, and the final `1`;
`|bits (n + 1)| ≤ ⌊log₂ (n + 1)⌋ + 1 ≤ logSpace n + 1` and `W ≥ 1`. -/
theorem length_cfgWord_le (s : ℕ) (C : Cfg N.k Bool N.State x) :
    (cfgWord s C).length ≤ codeK N * (s + logSpace x.length + 1) := by
  rw [length_cfgWord]
  have h1 : wP x.length ≤ logSpace x.length + 1 := by
    have e := length_bits_le_log (x.length + 1)
    have e2 : Nat.log 2 (x.length + 1) ≤ Nat.log 2 x.length + 1 := by
      rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos x.length with h | h
      · rw [h]; simp
      · have := Nat.log_mul_base (b := 2) (n := x.length) (by norm_num) (by omega)
        have := Nat.log_mono_right (b := 2) (show x.length + 1 ≤ x.length * 2 by omega)
        omega
    simp only [wP, logSpace]; omega
  have hW : 1 ≤ W N := by simp [W]
  simp only [codeK]
  have e1 : W N * (2 * s + 1) = 2 * (W N * s) + W N := by ring
  have e2 : (2 * W N + 2) * (s + logSpace x.length + 1) =
      2 * (W N * s) + 2 * (W N * logSpace x.length) + 2 * W N + 2 * s +
        2 * logSpace x.length + 2 := by ring
  rw [e1, e2]
  omega

/-- A word of `L` letters has value below `2 ^ L`. -/
lemma bitsVal_lt_two_pow (w : List Bool) : bitsVal w < 2 ^ w.length := by
  induction w with
  | nil => simp [bitsVal]
  | cons b w ih =>
    simp only [bitsVal, List.length_cons, pow_succ]
    cases b <;> simp <;> omega

/-- **The code is below `2 ^ (codeK N · (s + logSpace |x| + 1))`.** -/
theorem cfgCode_lt (s : ℕ) (C : Cfg N.k Bool N.State x) :
    cfgCode s C < 2 ^ (codeK N * (s + logSpace x.length + 1)) :=
  (bitsVal_lt_two_pow _).trans_le
    (Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) (length_cfgWord_le s C))

/-! ## Decoding -/

open Classical in
/-- **The decoder**: a window-bounded configuration with code `c` at radius `s`, if any
(chosen; it is determined up to the configuration-graph vertex,
`decodeCfg_cfgCode`). -/
noncomputable def decodeCfg (x : List Bool) (s c : ℕ) : Option (Cfg N.k Bool N.State x) :=
  if h : ∃ C : Cfg N.k Bool N.State x, Cfg.InWindow s C ∧ cfgCode s C = c then
    some (Classical.choose h)
  else none

/-- **Decoding a code recovers the vertex**: the decoder succeeds on the code of a
window-bounded configuration, with a window-bounded result of the same code and vertex.

**Proof sketch.** The chosen configuration has the same code, hence the same code word
(`bits_cfgCode`), hence the same vertex (`coreSum_eq_of_cfgWord_eq`). -/
theorem decodeCfg_cfgCode (s : ℕ) (C : Cfg N.k Bool N.State x) (hC : Cfg.InWindow s C) :
    ∃ D, decodeCfg x s (cfgCode s C) = some D ∧ Cfg.InWindow s D ∧ cfgCode s D = cfgCode s C ∧
      NDTM.coreSum D = NDTM.coreSum C := by
  classical
  have h : ∃ D : Cfg N.k Bool N.State x, Cfg.InWindow s D ∧ cfgCode s D = cfgCode s C :=
    ⟨C, hC, rfl⟩
  refine ⟨Classical.choose h, by simp [decodeCfg, h], (Classical.choose_spec h).1,
    (Classical.choose_spec h).2, ?_⟩
  apply coreSum_eq_of_cfgWord_eq (Classical.choose_spec h).1 hC
  rw [← bits_cfgCode, ← bits_cfgCode, (Classical.choose_spec h).2]

/-- The decoder fails exactly on numbers that are not codes. -/
theorem decodeCfg_eq_none (s c : ℕ) :
    decodeCfg (N := N) x s c = none ↔
      ¬ ∃ C : Cfg N.k Bool N.State x, Cfg.InWindow s C ∧ cfgCode s C = c := by
  classical
  unfold decodeCfg
  split_ifs with h <;> simp [h]

end Complexity.Codec
```

```
/-

Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Seyoon Ragavan
-/
import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.EquivFin
import Mathlib.Data.List.FinRange
import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Bits
import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Size
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.StateRenaming
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Robustness.SingleTape

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Machines as strings

[AB09, §1.4]: machines can be represented as binary strings, in such a way that
**(1)** every string represents some machine, and **(2)** every machine is represented
by infinitely many strings. This file provides the *code normal form* (`CodeTM`: one
work tape, binary alphabet, `Fin`-states — encodability requires fixing concrete
parameters, and by `Turing.FinTM.one_work_tape_binary` this normal form loses only a
quadratic factor), a fixed canonical serialization `CodeTM.serialize`, the
specification `MachineCode`/`EffectiveMachineCode` of a representation scheme, and the
self-delimiting pairing used by the universal machine.

## Design and deviations from [AB09]

* [AB09] fixes one concrete representation and standing conventions. We specify the
  representation *abstractly*, state the universal machine relative to it
  (`TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Universal`), and record the existence of a
  concrete scheme as a separate obligation.
* **The algebraic laws alone are not enough** (phase-3 audit, finding 1 and
  Argument A): a scheme satisfying only totality and padded round-trips may assign
  *noncomputable* meanings to codes — permuting the meanings of an honest scheme
  along an undecidable set preserves every law — and no universal machine can exist
  relative to such a scheme. Moreover requiring the scheme to canonize into *its own*
  encoding does not help (the pathological scheme's canonizer is computable). The
  effectivity contract must target a **fixed, scheme-independent** format: an
  `EffectiveMachineCode` carries a machine of this development computing
  `fun α => (decode α).serialize`, where `CodeTM.serialize` is the concrete
  serialization defined below. All universal-machine statements are relative to
  `EffectiveMachineCode`.
* Property (2) is stated as recovery under **`true`-padding of valid codes**
  (`decode_encode_pad`), the formal content of [AB09]'s "trailing 1s are ignored"
  convention; padding of *arbitrary* strings is deliberately not constrained.
  Property (1), totality, is enforced by `decode`'s type — this is a totality
  guarantee, not by itself a computability guarantee (audit finding 9).
* `CodeTM.serialize` records the state count, **the initial state** (audit finding 5:
  omitting it makes distinct machines collide), and the full transition table in a
  fixed enumeration order.

## Main definitions

* `Turing.CodeTM` — the code normal form; `Turing.CodeTM.toFinTM`;
  `Turing.CodeTM.serialize` — the fixed canonical serialization.
* `Turing.pairEncode` — self-delimiting pairing (first component doubled bitwise,
  separator `[false, true]`, second component verbatim); `Turing.dbl` — the doubling.
* `Turing.MachineCode` — the algebraic representation-scheme laws [AB09, §1.4].
* `Turing.EffectiveMachineCode` — a scheme together with an in-model machine
  computing `serialize ∘ decode`; the standing hypothesis of the universal machine.
* `Turing.pairDiagTM` — the diagonal pairing machine `α ↦ pairEncode α α` (MIG-1).
* `Turing.FinTM.toCodeTM` — the code normal form of a one-work-tape binary machine
  (MIG-1).

## Main results

* `Turing.MachineCode.decode_encode` — decoding a code recovers the machine.
* `Turing.pairEncode_injective` — the pairing is injective (aligned-pair parsing).
* `Turing.length_pairEncode`, `Turing.pairEncode_eq_dbl`, `Turing.pairDecode_eq_none`,
  `Turing.eq_pairEncode_of_pairDecode`, `Turing.pairEncode_replicate_inj` — the shape of
  the pairing, shared by the machine-side developments.
* `Turing.length_bits_le_self` — `|bits m| ≤ m`.
* `Turing.bits_two_pow_mul`, `Turing.bits_two_pow_eq_replicate` — the `Nat.bits` shift law
  `(2^j·m).bits = 0^j ++ m.bits` and its case `m = 1` (CH34-D4).
* `Turing.computesFunInTime_pairEncode_diag` — the diagonal pairing `α ↦ ⟨α, α⟩` is
  computable in linear time (the only code computation the `HALT` reduction needs).
  Its witness's spec is `Turing.pairDiagTM_computes` (MIG-1; sorried until the fill
  F-A).
* `Turing.FinTM.toCodeTM_computesInTime_iff` — the code normal form halts with the same
  outputs at the same times (MIG-1).
* `Turing.exists_codeTM` — every one-work-tape binary machine is equivalent to a
  coded machine (state relabeling).
* `Turing.exists_codeTM_spaceUsed` — the same coded machine also uses the same space at
  every time; `Turing.CodeTM.one_le_spaceUsed` — every coded run visits a cell.

The concrete parser/decoder realizing a scheme lives in
`TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.CodeParser`, and the existence of an effective
scheme (`Turing.exists_effectiveMachineCode`) is proved in
`TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.MathlibBridge`.
* `Turing.pairEncode_eq`, `Turing.unaryFin_eq` — the two encodings as equations, the
  specification API (user, 2026-10-16).
* `Turing.signBits_neg`/`_zero`/`_pos`, `Turing.optBoolBits_none`/`_some_false`/`_some_true`,
  `Turing.optOptBoolBits_none`/`_some_none`/`_some_false`/`_some_true`,
  `Turing.optStateBits_none`/`_some` — the record fields' encoders, case by case (the ND inventory
  API, round 2; gate 37, finding 1).

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§1.4, pp. 19-20.)
-/

namespace Turing

/-- A machine in *code normal form*: one work tape, binary alphabet, and states drawn
from a canonical nonempty finite type `Fin (numStates + 1)`. [AB09, §1.4] -/
structure CodeTM where
  /-- one less than the number of states (so the state space is never empty) -/
  numStates : ℕ
  /-- the underlying machine -/
  tm : MultiTapeTM 1 Bool (Fin (numStates + 1))

/-- The bundled machine of a coded machine. -/
def CodeTM.toFinTM (M : CodeTM) : FinTM Bool where
  k := 1
  State := Fin (M.numStates + 1)
  tm := M.tm

/-- The bundled form of a coded machine has exactly one work tape. -/
@[simp]
lemma CodeTM.toFinTM_k (M : CodeTM) : M.toFinTM.k = 1 := rfl

/-- Self-delimiting pairing of two binary strings: the **first** string with every bit
doubled, then the separator `[false, true]`, then the second string verbatim. Parsing
reads aligned two-bit blocks: `00`/`11` are data, the first aligned `01` is the
separator (a `01` can only occur unaligned inside doubled data), and the suffix is the
second component. The universal machine's input convention is `pairEncode α x` —
**code first, input second**, deviating from [AB09]'s `⟨x, α⟩` order so that the
simulation's startup cost is independent of the input (phase-3 audit, finding 2 and
Argument B: with the input first, no bound `C · (t + 1)` with `C` independent of `x`
can hold). -/
def pairEncode (x α : List Bool) : List Bool :=
  (x.flatMap fun b => [b, b]) ++ [false, true] ++ α

/-- **The pairing as an equation** (the specification API, user 2026-10-16): the code doubled,
the separator `false, true`, then the second word. -/
theorem pairEncode_eq (x α : List Bool) :
    pairEncode x α = (x.flatMap fun b => [b, b]) ++ [false, true] ++ α :=
  rfl

/-- Parse aligned doubled bits until the separator, leaving its suffix untouched. -/
def pairDecode : List Bool → Option (List Bool × List Bool)
  | false :: false :: rest => (pairDecode rest).map fun p => (false :: p.1, p.2)
  | true :: true :: rest => (pairDecode rest).map fun p => (true :: p.1, p.2)
  | false :: true :: rest => some ([], rest)
  | _ => none

/-- The aligned parser recovers both components, by induction on the first word. -/
lemma pairDecode_pairEncode (x α : List Bool) :
    pairDecode (pairEncode x α) = some (x, α) := by
  induction x with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons b x ih =>
    have h := congrArg (Option.map fun p : List Bool × List Bool => (b :: p.1, p.2)) ih
    cases b <;> simpa [pairEncode, pairDecode] using h

/-- The pairing is injective.

**Proof sketch** (phase-3 audit, Argument D). The aligned two-bit parser recovers the
components: read blocks of two from the left; `00` yields `false`, `11` yields `true`,
and the first aligned `01` is the separator — no doubled bit produces an aligned `01`.
The remaining suffix is the second component verbatim. This parser is a left inverse
of the pairing, and a function with a left inverse is injective. Empty components are
unproblematic (`pairEncode [] α = [false, true] ++ α`). -/
theorem pairEncode_injective :
    Function.Injective fun p : List Bool × List Bool => pairEncode p.1 p.2 := by
  intro p q h
  have := congrArg pairDecode h
  simpa only [pairDecode_pairEncode, Prod.mk.eta, Option.some.injEq] using this

/-! ### Shape of the pairing

Generic list facts about `pairEncode` and `pairDecode`, shared by the machine-side
developments (the time hierarchy, the polynomial hierarchy, logspace machines, and
the circuit-evaluation machines). -/

/-- A word with every bit written twice — the first component of `Turing.pairEncode`. -/
def dbl (w : List Bool) : List Bool := w.flatMap fun b => [b, b]

/-- Doubling the empty word gives the empty word. -/
@[simp] lemma dbl_nil : dbl [] = [] := rfl

/-- Doubling `b :: w` is `b b` followed by doubling `w`. -/
@[simp] lemma dbl_cons (b : Bool) (w : List Bool) : dbl (b :: w) = b :: b :: dbl w := rfl

/-- Doubling a word doubles its length. -/
@[simp] lemma length_dbl (w : List Bool) : (dbl w).length = 2 * w.length := by
  induction w with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons b w ih => simp [ih]; ring

/-- Both copies of bit `c` of a doubled word read `w[c]`. -/
lemma getElem?_dbl (w : List Bool) (c : ℕ) (hc : c < w.length) (p : Bool) :
    (dbl w)[2 * c + p.toNat]? = some w[c] := by
  induction w generalizing c with
  | nil => simp at hc
  | cons b w ih =>
    cases c with
    | zero => cases p <;> simp
    | succ c =>
      have := ih c (by simpa using hc)
      simp only [dbl_cons, List.getElem_cons_succ]
      rw [show 2 * (c + 1) + p.toNat = (2 * c + p.toNat) + 1 + 1 by ring]
      simpa using this

/-- `pairEncode x y` is the doubled first word, the separator `[false, true]`, and the
second word. -/
lemma pairEncode_eq_dbl (x y : List Bool) : pairEncode x y = dbl x ++ [false, true] ++ y :=
  rfl

/-- The length of a pair: `|pairEncode x y| = 2|x| + 2 + |y|`. -/
theorem length_pairEncode (x y : List Bool) :
    (pairEncode x y).length = 2 * x.length + 2 + y.length := by
  simp [pairEncode_eq_dbl]
  omega

/-- A string that is not a pair is a doubled word followed by a malformed tail: the end
of the string, a lone bit, or the aligned pair `10`.

**Proof sketch.** Functional induction along `pairDecode`: aligned `00`/`11` pairs extend
the doubled prefix; in the remaining case the string matches none of `00`, `11`, `01`,
so it is empty, a single bit, or starts with `10`. -/
theorem pairDecode_eq_none (z : List Bool) (h : pairDecode z = none) :
    ∃ w tail, z = dbl w ++ tail ∧
      (tail = [] ∨ (∃ b, tail = [b]) ∨ ∃ r, tail = true :: false :: r) := by
  induction z using pairDecode.induct with
  | case1 xs ih =>
    have h' : pairDecode xs = none := by simpa [pairDecode] using h
    obtain ⟨w, tail, hw, ht⟩ := ih h'
    exact ⟨false :: w, tail, by simp [hw], ht⟩
  | case2 xs ih =>
    have h' : pairDecode xs = none := by simpa [pairDecode] using h
    obtain ⟨w, tail, hw, ht⟩ := ih h'
    exact ⟨true :: w, tail, by simp [hw], ht⟩
  | case3 xs => simp [pairDecode] at h
  | case4 xs h₁ h₂ h₃ =>
    refine ⟨[], xs, by simp, ?_⟩
    rcases xs with _ | ⟨b, _ | ⟨c, r⟩⟩
    · exact Or.inl rfl
    · exact Or.inr (Or.inl ⟨b, rfl⟩)
    · cases b <;> cases c
      · exact absurd rfl (h₁ r)
      · exact absurd rfl (h₃ r)
      · exact Or.inr (Or.inr ⟨r, rfl⟩)
      · exact absurd rfl (h₂ r)

/-- A successfully decoded string is the pairing of its components.

**Proof sketch.** Functional induction along `pairDecode`, inverting
`pairDecode_pairEncode` one aligned pair at a time. -/
theorem eq_pairEncode_of_pairDecode (z a b : List Bool) (h : pairDecode z = some (a, b)) :
    z = pairEncode a b := by
  induction z using pairDecode.induct generalizing a with
  | case1 xs ih =>
    cases hr : pairDecode xs with
    | none => simp [pairDecode, hr] at h
    | some p =>
      rcases p with ⟨ys, tail⟩
      simp only [pairDecode, hr, Option.map_some, Option.some.injEq, Prod.mk.injEq] at h
      rcases h with ⟨rfl, rfl⟩
      simpa [pairEncode] using congrArg (fun zs => false :: false :: zs) (ih ys hr)
  | case2 xs ih =>
    cases hr : pairDecode xs with
    | none => simp [pairDecode, hr] at h
    | some p =>
      rcases p with ⟨ys, tail⟩
      simp only [pairDecode, hr, Option.map_some, Option.some.injEq, Prod.mk.injEq] at h
      rcases h with ⟨rfl, rfl⟩
      simpa [pairEncode] using congrArg (fun zs => true :: true :: zs) (ih ys hr)
  | case3 xs =>
    simp only [pairDecode, Option.some.injEq, Prod.mk.injEq] at h
    rcases h with ⟨rfl, rfl⟩
    rfl
  | case4 xs h₁ h₂ h₃ => simp [pairDecode] at h

/-- A unary-first pair `⟨1ⁿ, u⟩` determines both `n` and `u`. -/
lemma pairEncode_replicate_inj {n n' : ℕ} {u u' : List Bool}
    (h : pairEncode (List.replicate n true) u = pairEncode (List.replicate n' true) u') :
    n = n' ∧ u = u' := by
  have := pairEncode_injective (a₁ := (List.replicate n true, u))
    (a₂ := (List.replicate n' true, u')) h
  simp only [Prod.mk.injEq] at this
  obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := this
  exact ⟨by simpa using congrArg List.length h1, h2⟩

/-- The binary expansion of `m` has at most `m` bits. -/
lemma length_bits_le_self (m : ℕ) : m.bits.length ≤ m := by
  rw [Nat.size_eq_bits_len]
  exact Nat.size_le.mpr Nat.lt_two_pow_self

/-- **The `Nat.bits` shift law**: multiplying a positive `m` by `2 ^ j`
prepends `j` low zero bits to its little-endian binary expansion,
`(2^j·m).bits = 0^j ++ m.bits`. (Positivity is needed: `Nat.bits 0 = []`.)
The public home of the law, promoted per the fills-6 request F6-1(a)
(CH34-D4).

**Proof sketch.** Induct on `j`. A positive number stays positive after
multiplication by a power of two, and doubling a nonzero number prepends one
low zero bit to its expansion; induction counts the prepended zeros. -/
theorem bits_two_pow_mul (j m : ℕ) (hm : 0 < m) :
    (2 ^ j * m).bits = List.replicate j false ++ m.bits := by
  induction j with
  | zero => simp
  | succ j ih =>
    rw [pow_succ', mul_assoc, Nat.bit0_bits _ (Nat.mul_pos (Nat.two_pow_pos j) hm).ne']
    simp only [ih, List.replicate_succ, List.cons_append]

/-- The little-endian binary expansion of `2 ^ n` is `n` zero bits followed by
one high bit: `(2^n).bits = 0^n 1`. The case `m = 1` of
`Turing.bits_two_pow_mul`, since the expansion of `1` is the single bit `1`. -/
theorem bits_two_pow_eq_replicate (n : ℕ) :
    (2 ^ n).bits = List.replicate n false ++ [true] := by
  simpa using bits_two_pow_mul n 1 Nat.one_pos

/-- **The diagonal pairing machine**. A six-state machine with no work tapes that, on input `α`,
writes each symbol of `α` twice, then the separator `false, true`, rewinds the input, and copies `α`
once more, so that it outputs `pairEncode α α`. It is also the witness of
`Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_pairDup` (consolidation: Primitives' private `pairDupTM`, which
computes the same function, retires). [AB09, proof of Theorem 1.11: the self-application input of
the `HALT` reduction] -/
def pairDiagTM : FinTM Bool where
  k := 0
  State := Fin 6
  tm :=
    { q₀ := 0
      tr := fun q inp _ =>
        match q with
        | 0 => match inp with
          | some b => ⟨.zero, fun i => i.elim0, some b, some 1⟩
          | none => ⟨.zero, fun i => i.elim0, some false, some 2⟩
        | 1 => ⟨.pos, fun i => i.elim0, inp, some 0⟩
        | 2 => ⟨.zero, fun i => i.elim0, some true, some 3⟩
        | 3 => ⟨.neg, fun i => i.elim0, none, some 4⟩
        | 4 => match inp with
          | some _ => ⟨.neg, fun i => i.elim0, none, some 4⟩
          | none => ⟨.pos, fun i => i.elim0, none, some 5⟩
        | _ => match inp with
          | some b => ⟨.pos, fun i => i.elim0, some b, some 5⟩
          | none => ⟨.zero, fun i => i.elim0, none, none⟩ }

/-- A pairing-machine configuration, with its vacuous work-tape fields suppressed. -/
private def pairDiagCfg (x : List Bool) (q : Option (Fin 6))
    (p : Fin (x.length + 2)) (out : List Bool) : Cfg 0 Bool (Fin 6) x :=
  ⟨q, p, fun i => i.elim0, fun i => i.elim0, out⟩

/-- One live transition of the pairing controller, given its scanned input symbol. -/
private lemma pairDiag_step (x : List Bool) (q : Fin 6)
    (p : Fin (x.length + 2)) (out : List Bool) (b : Option Bool)
    (hb : (pairDiagCfg x (some q) p out).inputSymbol = b) :
    pairDiagTM.tm.step (pairDiagCfg x (some q) p out) =
      let a := pairDiagTM.tm.tr q b (fun i => i.elim0)
      pairDiagCfg x a.state (moveInputPos p a.inputTape) (out ++ a.output.toList) := by
  change (pairDiagTM.tm.tr q (pairDiagCfg x (some q) p out).inputSymbol
    (pairDiagCfg x (some q) p out).workTapeSymbols).apply _ = _
  rw [hb]
  exact Cfg.ext_zero_tapes rfl rfl rfl

/-- At position `j + 1`, the pairing machine reads the `j`-th input bit. -/
private lemma pairDiag_inner (x : List Bool) (q : Option (Fin 6)) (out : List Bool)
    (j : ℕ) (hj : j < x.length) :
    (pairDiagCfg x q ⟨j + 1, by omega⟩ out).inputSymbol = some x[j] :=
  inputSymbolInner j (by simp only [pairDiagCfg]; omega) hj

/-- At the right boundary the pairing machine reads blank, also on empty input. -/
private lemma pairDiag_right (x : List Bool) (q : Option (Fin 6)) (out : List Bool) :
    (pairDiagCfg x q ⟨x.length + 1, by omega⟩ out).inputSymbol = none := by
  simp [pairDiagCfg, Cfg.inputSymbol, Fin.ext_iff]

/-- After `2t` transitions, the first pass has doubled exactly the first `t` bits.

**Proof sketch.** Induct on `t`. Each bit is first emitted without moving and then
emitted again while moving right. The two emissions extend the doubled prefix. -/
private lemma pairDiag_double (x : List Bool) : ∀ t, (ht : t ≤ x.length) →
    pairDiagTM.tm.runFrom (pairDiagTM.tm.initCfg x) (2 * t) =
      pairDiagCfg x (some 0) ⟨t + 1, by omega⟩ ((x.take t).flatMap fun b => [b, b]) := by
  intro t
  induction t with
  | zero =>
    intro _
    apply Cfg.ext_zero_tapes <;> simp [pairDiagTM, pairDiagCfg, MultiTapeTM.runFrom]
  | succ t ih =>
    intro ht
    rw [show 2 * (t + 1) = 2 * t + 1 + 1 by omega,
      MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', ih (by omega)]
    rw [pairDiag_step _ _ _ _ _ (pairDiag_inner x (some 0) _ t (by omega))]
    simp only [pairDiagTM, SignType.zero_eq_zero, moveInputPos_zero, Option.toList_some]
    rw [pairDiag_step _ _ _ _ _ (pairDiag_inner x (some 1) _ t (by omega))]
    simp only [pairDiagTM, Option.toList_some]
    rw [moveInputPos_pos_of_ne_right _ (by change t + 1 ≠ x.length + 1; omega)]
    apply Cfg.ext_zero_tapes
    · rfl
    · rfl
    · change (((x.take t).flatMap fun b => [b, b]) ++ [x[t]]) ++ [x[t]] =
        (x.take (t + 1)).flatMap fun b => [b, b]
      rw [List.take_succ, List.getElem?_eq_getElem (by omega)]
      simp only [Option.toList_some, List.flatMap_append, List.flatMap_cons,
        List.flatMap_nil, List.append_nil, List.append_assoc, List.cons_append, List.nil_append]

/-- Rewinding from position `j ≤ n` takes `j + 1` steps and preserves the output.

**Proof sketch.** At position zero, move right and enter the copy state. At a
positive position at most `n`, the read is a symbol, so move left and apply the
induction hypothesis. The preceding unconditional left step reaches this range. -/
private lemma pairDiag_rewind (x out : List Bool) : ∀ j, (hj : j ≤ x.length) →
    pairDiagTM.tm.runFrom (pairDiagCfg x (some 4) ⟨j, by omega⟩ out) (j + 1) =
      pairDiagCfg x (some 5) 1 out := by
  intro j
  induction j with
  | zero =>
    intro _
    rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', MultiTapeTM.runFrom_zero,
      pairDiag_step _ _ _ _ none (by simp [pairDiagCfg, Cfg.inputSymbol])]
    simp only [pairDiagTM, Option.toList_none, List.append_nil]
    rw [moveInputPos_pos_of_ne_right _ (by simp)]
    apply Cfg.ext_zero_tapes
    · rfl
    · apply Fin.ext; simp [pairDiagCfg]
    · rfl
  | succ j ih =>
    intro hj
    rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step,
      pairDiag_step _ _ _ _ _ (pairDiag_inner x (some 4) out j (by omega))]
    simp only [pairDiagTM, Option.toList_none, List.append_nil]
    rw [moveInputPos_neg_of_ne_left _ (by simp [Fin.ext_iff])]
    simpa using ih (by omega)

/-- The second pass appends the first `t` input bits in `t` transitions.

**Proof sketch.** Induct on `t`, reading at position `t + 1`, appending that bit,
and moving right. The previously emitted doubled word and separator are preserved. -/
private lemma pairDiag_copy (x out : List Bool) : ∀ t, (ht : t ≤ x.length) →
    pairDiagTM.tm.runFrom (pairDiagCfg x (some 5) 1 out) t =
      pairDiagCfg x (some 5) ⟨t + 1, by omega⟩ (out ++ x.take t) := by
  intro t
  induction t with
  | zero =>
    intro _
    apply Cfg.ext_zero_tapes <;> simp [pairDiagCfg]
  | succ t ih =>
    intro ht
    rw [MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', ih (by omega),
      pairDiag_step _ _ _ _ _ (pairDiag_inner x (some 5) _ t (by omega))]
    simp only [pairDiagTM, Option.toList_some]
    rw [moveInputPos_pos_of_ne_right _ (by change t + 1 ≠ x.length + 1; omega)]
    apply Cfg.ext_zero_tapes
    · rfl
    · rfl
    · change (out ++ x.take t) ++ [x[t]] = out ++ x.take (t + 1)
      rw [List.take_succ, List.getElem?_eq_getElem (by omega)]
      simp only [Option.toList_some, List.append_assoc]

/-- Two stationary separator emissions followed by the unconditional first left move.

**Proof sketch.** At the right blank, states 0 and 2 emit `false` and `true`.
State 3 then moves from position `n + 1` to `n`, without emitting a bit. -/
private lemma pairDiag_separator (x out : List Bool) :
    pairDiagTM.tm.runFrom
      (pairDiagCfg x (some 0) ⟨x.length + 1, by omega⟩ out) 3 =
      pairDiagCfg x (some 4) ⟨x.length, by omega⟩ (out ++ [false, true]) := by
  rw [show 3 = (0 + 1) + 1 + 1 from rfl,
    MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step',
    MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', MultiTapeTM.runFrom_zero]
  rw [pairDiag_step _ _ _ _ _ (pairDiag_right x (some 0) out)]
  simp only [pairDiagTM, SignType.zero_eq_zero, moveInputPos_zero, Option.toList_some]
  rw [pairDiag_step _ _ _ _ _ (pairDiag_right x (some 2) _)]
  simp only [pairDiagTM, SignType.zero_eq_zero, moveInputPos_zero, Option.toList_some]
  rw [pairDiag_step _ _ _ _ _ (pairDiag_right x (some 3) _)]
  simp only [pairDiagTM, Option.toList_none, List.append_nil]
  rw [moveInputPos_neg_of_ne_left _ (by simp [Fin.ext_iff])]
  apply Cfg.ext_zero_tapes <;> simp [pairDiagCfg, List.append_assoc]

/-- The complete pairing run is halted with the required output by step `4n + 5`.

**Proof sketch.** Chain the doubled pass (`2n`), the two separator steps and first
left move (`3`), the rewind from position `n` (`n + 1`), the copy (`n`), and the
halting transition (`1`). Each equality records the whole configuration. -/
private lemma pairDiag_run (x : List Bool) :
    pairDiagTM.tm.runFrom (pairDiagTM.tm.initCfg x) (4 * x.length + 5) =
      pairDiagCfg x none ⟨x.length + 1, by omega⟩ (pairEncode x x) := by
  have hd := pairDiag_double x x.length (le_refl _)
  simp only [List.take_length] at hd
  have hr : pairDiagTM.tm.runFrom (pairDiagTM.tm.initCfg x) (3 * x.length + 4) =
      pairDiagCfg x (some 5) 1 ((x.flatMap fun b => [b, b]) ++ [false, true]) := by
    rw [show 3 * x.length + 4 = 2 * x.length + (3 + (x.length + 1)) by omega,
      MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, hd, MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, pairDiag_separator,
      pairDiag_rewind x _ x.length (le_refl _)]
  have hc : pairDiagTM.tm.runFrom (pairDiagTM.tm.initCfg x) (4 * x.length + 4) =
      pairDiagCfg x (some 5) ⟨x.length + 1, by omega⟩ (pairEncode x x) := by
    rw [show 4 * x.length + 4 = (3 * x.length + 4) + x.length by omega,
      MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, hr, pairDiag_copy x _ x.length (le_refl _)]
    simp only [List.take_length, pairEncode]
  rw [show 4 * x.length + 5 = (4 * x.length + 4) + 1 by omega,
    MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', hc,
    pairDiag_step _ _ _ _ _ (pairDiag_right x (some 5) _)]
  simp only [pairDiagTM, SignType.zero_eq_zero, moveInputPos_zero, Option.toList_none, List.append_nil]

/-- **The diagonal pairing machine's time**. On input `α` the diagonal pairing machine halts within
`4|α| + 5` steps with output `pairEncode α α`.

**Proof sketch.** The `have h` of today's `computesFunInTime_pairEncode_diag`, from the private
`pairDiag_run`: the doubling pass takes `2|α|` steps, the two separator steps and the first left
move `3`, the rewind `|α| + 1`, the copy `|α|`, and the halting transition `1`. -/
theorem pairDiagTM_computes (x : List Bool) :
    pairDiagTM.ComputesInTime x (pairEncode x x) (4 * x.length + 5) := by
  sorry

/-- The diagonal pairing `α ↦ pairEncode α α` — the self-application input of the
`HALT` reduction [AB09, proof of Theorem 1.11] — is computable in linear time. This
is the *only* computation on codes that reduction needs (phase-3 audit, round 2,
Argument F): `encode` itself is never computed by any machine of this development.

**Proof sketch.** Two sweeps of the input with a constant number of states. Pass one
walks the input left to right emitting each bit twice — one emitted symbol per
transition, so two steps per bit: emit staying put, emit moving right; on reading the
right boundary blank it emits the separator `false`, `true` (two steps) and rewinds
the input head to the start (one step left, then left while reading a symbol, then
one step right — the clamp at position `0` makes this safe, including on empty
input). Pass two walks the input again emitting each bit once, and halts on the
boundary blank. Total on inputs of length `n`: `2n` (doubled pass) `+ 2` (separator)
`+ (n + 2)` (rewind) `+ n` (second pass) `+ 1` (halt) `= 4n + 5 ≤ 6 · (n + 1)`
(phase-4 audit, finding 1: an earlier `3n + 6` figure undercounted the doubled
pass), absorbed as `c * (n + 1)`. -/
theorem computesFunInTime_pairEncode_diag :
    ∃ (M : FinTM Bool) (c : ℕ),
      M.ComputesFunInTime (fun α => pairEncode α α) fun n => c * (n + 1) := by
  refine ⟨pairDiagTM, 6, fun x => ?_⟩
  have h : pairDiagTM.ComputesInTime x (pairEncode x x) (4 * x.length + 5) := by
    refine ⟨_, ?_, ?_, rfl⟩
    · rw [pairDiag_run]; rfl
    · rw [pairDiag_run]; rfl
  exact h.mono (by change 4 * x.length + 5 ≤ 6 * (x.length + 1); omega)

section Serialize

/-- Fixed two-bit serialization of a head move. -/
def signBits : SignType → List Bool
  | .neg => [true, true]
  | .zero => [false, false]
  | .pos => [true, false]

/-- **A left move's bits** (the ND inventory API, round 2; gate 37, finding 1):
`signBits .neg = [true, true]`. -/
theorem signBits_neg : signBits .neg = [true, true] := rfl

/-- **A stay's bits** (the ND inventory API, round 2; gate 37, finding 1):
`signBits .zero = [false, false]`. -/
theorem signBits_zero : signBits .zero = [false, false] := rfl

/-- **A right move's bits** (the ND inventory API, round 2; gate 37, finding 1):
`signBits .pos = [true, false]`. -/
theorem signBits_pos : signBits .pos = [true, false] := rfl

/-- Fixed two-bit serialization of an optional bit. -/
def optBoolBits : Option Bool → List Bool
  | none => [false, false]
  | some false => [true, false]
  | some true => [true, true]

/-- **No bit's bits** (the ND inventory API, round 2; gate 37, finding 1):
`optBoolBits none = [false, false]`. -/
theorem optBoolBits_none : optBoolBits none = [false, false] := rfl

/-- **The bit `false`'s bits** (the ND inventory API, round 2; gate 37, finding 1):
`optBoolBits (some false) = [true, false]`. -/
theorem optBoolBits_some_false : optBoolBits (some false) = [true, false] := rfl

/-- **The bit `true`'s bits** (the ND inventory API, round 2; gate 37, finding 1):
`optBoolBits (some true) = [true, true]`. -/
theorem optBoolBits_some_true : optBoolBits (some true) = [true, true] := rfl

/-- Fixed two-bit serialization of an optional write (which may itself write blank). -/
def optOptBoolBits : Option (Option Bool) → List Bool
  | none => [false, false]
  | some none => [false, true]
  | some (some false) => [true, false]
  | some (some true) => [true, true]

/-- **No write's bits** (the ND inventory API, round 2; gate 37, finding 1):
`optOptBoolBits none = [false, false]`. -/
theorem optOptBoolBits_none : optOptBoolBits none = [false, false] := rfl

/-- **A blank write's bits** (the ND inventory API, round 2; gate 37, finding 1):
`optOptBoolBits (some none) = [false, true]`. -/
theorem optOptBoolBits_some_none : optOptBoolBits (some none) = [false, true] := rfl

/-- **Writing `false`, in bits** (the ND inventory API, round 2; gate 37, finding 1):
`optOptBoolBits (some (some false)) = [true, false]`. -/
theorem optOptBoolBits_some_false : optOptBoolBits (some (some false)) = [true, false] := rfl

/-- **Writing `true`, in bits** (the ND inventory API, round 2; gate 37, finding 1):
`optOptBoolBits (some (some true)) = [true, true]`. -/
theorem optOptBoolBits_some_true : optOptBoolBits (some (some true)) = [true, true] := rfl

/-- Self-delimiting unary serialization of a state index. -/
def unaryFin {n : ℕ} (s : Fin n) : List Bool :=
  List.replicate (s : ℕ) true ++ [false]

/-- **The unary state word as an equation** (the specification API, user 2026-10-16): `s`
`true`s, then the delimiter `false`. -/
theorem unaryFin_eq {n : ℕ} (s : Fin n) : unaryFin s = List.replicate (s : ℕ) true ++ [false] :=
  rfl

/-- Serialization of an optional successor state (`none` = halt). -/
def optStateBits {n : ℕ} : Option (Fin n) → List Bool
  | none => [false]
  | some s => true :: unaryFin s

/-- **Halting's bits** (the ND inventory API, round 2; gate 37, finding 1):
`optStateBits none = [false]`. -/
theorem optStateBits_none {n : ℕ} : optStateBits (none : Option (Fin n)) = [false] := rfl

/-- **A successor state's bits** (the ND inventory API, round 2; gate 37, finding 1):
`optStateBits (some s) = true :: unaryFin s`. -/
theorem optStateBits_some {n : ℕ} (s : Fin n) : optStateBits (some s) = true :: unaryFin s := rfl

/-- Serialization of one transition record. -/
def actionBits {n : ℕ} (a : Action 1 Bool (Fin (n + 1))) : List Bool :=
  signBits a.inputTape ++ optOptBoolBits (a.workTapes 0).1 ++
    signBits (a.workTapes 0).2 ++ optBoolBits a.output ++ optStateBits a.state

/-- The **fixed, scheme-independent** canonical serialization of a coded machine: the
state count (self-delimiting via `pairEncode`'s doubled-bit region), then the initial
state (audit finding 5: it must be recorded — machines with equal tables and
different initial states differ), then the full transition table in the fixed
enumeration order (states in `Fin` order; input read and work read each ranging over
`none`, `some false`, `some true`). This is the target format of
`EffectiveMachineCode.canonizer`, which is what ties a scheme's `decode` to effective
semantics (audit finding 1). -/
def CodeTM.serialize (M : CodeTM) : List Bool :=
  pairEncode (Nat.bits M.numStates)
    (unaryFin M.tm.q₀ ++
      (List.finRange (M.numStates + 1)).flatMap fun q =>
        ([none, some false, some true] : List (Option Bool)).flatMap fun inp =>
          ([none, some false, some true] : List (Option Bool)).flatMap fun w =>
            actionBits (M.tm.tr q inp fun _ => w))

end Serialize

/-- The algebraic laws of a representation scheme for coded machines [AB09, §1.4]: a
total decoding (every string represents some machine — property 1), an encoding, and
recovery of the machine from its code under arbitrary `true`-padding (hence every
machine has infinitely many representations — property 2).

These laws alone do **not** support universal simulation — see the module docstring
and `Turing.EffectiveMachineCode`. -/
structure MachineCode where
  /-- encode a machine as a binary string, `⌞M⌟` -/
  encode : CodeTM → List Bool
  /-- decode any binary string to a machine (total by type: property 1) -/
  decode : List Bool → CodeTM
  /-- a code followed by any amount of `true`-padding decodes to the machine
  (property 2: infinitely many representations) -/
  decode_encode_pad : ∀ M m, decode (encode M ++ List.replicate m true) = M

/-- Decoding a code recovers the machine ([AB09, §1.4]; padding by zero symbols). -/
theorem MachineCode.decode_encode (c : MachineCode) (M : CodeTM) :
    c.decode (c.encode M) = M := by
  simpa using c.decode_encode_pad M 0

/-- An *effective* representation scheme: the algebraic laws together with a machine
of this development that computes the fixed serialization of the decoded machine,
within some time bound depending only on the code's length.

The target `CodeTM.serialize` is scheme-independent, which is essential: requiring
only a canonizer into the scheme's *own* `encode` is still satisfied by the
noncomputable-meaning pathology of audit Argument A, whereas computing
`serialize ∘ decode` for that pathology would decide an undecidable set, so no such
machine exists and the pathology is excluded. -/
structure EffectiveMachineCode extends MachineCode where
  /-- a machine computing the fixed serialization of the decoded machine -/
  canonizer : FinTM Bool
  /-- the canonizer's time bound (arbitrary here; universal-machine constants absorb
  its value at each fixed code) -/
  canonizerTime : ℕ → ℕ
  /-- the canonizer computes `serialize ∘ decode` -/
  canonizer_computes :
    canonizer.ComputesFunInTime (fun α => (decode α).serialize) canonizerTime

/-- **A coded run visits at least one cell.** Every run of a coded machine, at every time,
has visited at least one work cell: its one work head starts somewhere. So every qualifying
budget `s` of `Complexity.space_universal` is positive, which is what lets its addend-free bound
`C · s` absorb a ruler of the header's length (the RD-3 statement gate's row-1 calculation).

**Proof sketch.** The visited set of tape `0` contains the head's initial position, and it
is one summand of the space. -/
theorem CodeTM.one_le_spaceUsed (M : CodeTM) (x : List Bool) (t : ℕ) :
    1 ≤ M.toFinTM.tm.spaceUsed (M.toFinTM.tm.initCfg x) t := by
  let i₀ : Fin M.toFinTM.k := ⟨0, by simp⟩
  have hne : (M.toFinTM.tm.visitedByTapeHead (M.toFinTM.tm.initCfg x) t i₀).Nonempty :=
    ⟨_, Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨0, Finset.mem_range.mpr (Nat.succ_pos t), rfl⟩⟩
  exact (Finset.card_pos.mpr hne).trans_le
    (M.toFinTM.tm.spaceUsedByTape_le_spaceUsed _ t i₀)

/-- **Renaming a machine's states preserves its computations.** Renaming the states of a bundled
machine along an equivalence `e` gives a machine that halts on the same inputs at the same times,
with the same outputs.

**Proof sketch.** The renamed machine's initialized runs are the original runs with renamed
states (`Turing.MultiTapeTM.relabelState_runFrom_init`), and renaming changes neither halting nor
the output. -/
theorem FinTM.computesInTime_relabelState {Symbol : Type} (M : FinTM Symbol) {Q : Type}
    [Fintype Q] [DecidableEq Q] (e : M.State ≃ Q) (x output : List Symbol) (t : ℕ) :
    (FinTM.mk (k := M.k) (State := Q) (M.tm.relabelState e)).ComputesInTime x output t ↔
      M.ComputesInTime x output t := by
  rw [FinTM.computesInTime_iff, FinTM.computesInTime_iff]
  dsimp only
  rw [MultiTapeTM.relabelState_runFrom_init, Cfg.mapState_state, Cfg.mapState_output,
    Option.map_eq_none_iff]

/-- **A machine's states as an initial segment of `ℕ`.** The states of a bundled machine are in
bijection with `Fin (n + 1)` for `n = |State| - 1`: the state type is finite, and inhabited by the
start state. Noncomputable, through `Fintype.equivFinOfCardEq`. -/
noncomputable def FinTM.stateEquivFin {Symbol : Type} (M : FinTM Symbol) :
    M.State ≃ Fin (Fintype.card M.State - 1 + 1) :=
  Fintype.equivFinOfCardEq (by
    have : 0 < Fintype.card M.State := Fintype.card_pos_iff.mpr ⟨M.tm.q₀⟩
    omega)

/-- `Turing.FinTM.stateEquivFin` is the bijection that `Fintype.equivFinOfCardEq` gives for the
state count, which the start state makes positive (its defining equation). -/
theorem FinTM.stateEquivFin_eq {Symbol : Type} (M : FinTM Symbol) :
    M.stateEquivFin = Fintype.equivFinOfCardEq (by
      have : 0 < Fintype.card M.State := Fintype.card_pos_iff.mpr ⟨M.tm.q₀⟩
      omega) :=
  rfl

/-- **The space-faithful coding step.** Every one-work-tape binary machine `M` is equivalent
to a coded machine `M'` that halts with the same outputs at the same times
(`Turing.exists_codeTM`'s clause) **and uses the same space at every time**. This is the space
clause of the coding step named by `Complexity.space_hierarchy`'s sketch. [AB09, §1.4]

**Proof sketch.** `State` carries `Fintype`/`DecidableEq` instances and is inhabited by `q₀`,
so `Fintype.equivFinOfCardEq` gives an equivalence with `Fin (|Q| - 1 + 1)`. Relabel the states
along it (`Turing.MultiTapeTM.relabelState`): by `Turing.MultiTapeTM.relabelState_runFrom_init`
the relabelled run is the original run with renamed states, so halting and outputs correspond
at every time, and the space clause is `Turing.MultiTapeTM.relabelState_spaceUsed`. The
tape-count cast uses `hk : M.k = 1`, eliminated after destructuring the bundle. -/
theorem exists_codeTM_spaceUsed (M : FinTM Bool) (hk : M.k = 1) :
    ∃ M' : CodeTM,
      (∀ (x output : List Bool) (t : ℕ),
        M'.toFinTM.ComputesInTime x output t ↔ M.ComputesInTime x output t) ∧
      ∀ (x : List Bool) (t : ℕ),
        M'.toFinTM.tm.spaceUsed (M'.toFinTM.tm.initCfg x) t =
          M.tm.spaceUsed (M.tm.initCfg x) t := by
  rcases M with @⟨k, Q, hQ, dQ, tm⟩
  dsimp only at hk
  subst k
  let M₀ : FinTM Bool := ⟨1, Q, tm⟩
  exact ⟨⟨Fintype.card Q - 1, tm.relabelState M₀.stateEquivFin⟩,
    M₀.computesInTime_relabelState M₀.stateEquivFin,
    fun x t => MultiTapeTM.relabelState_spaceUsed tm M₀.stateEquivFin x t⟩

/-- **The code normal form of a one-work-tape machine**. For a binary machine `M` with one work
tape, the coded machine with `|Q| - 1` as its state index bound, whose transition function is `M`'s
transported along the canonical bijection `Q ≃ Fin |Q|` (`Turing.FinTM.stateEquivFin`; `Q` is
inhabited by the start state). [AB09, §1.4] Noncomputable, through `Fintype.equivFinOfCardEq`. -/
noncomputable def FinTM.toCodeTM : (M : FinTM Bool) → M.k = 1 → CodeTM
  | @FinTM.mk _ _ Q _hQ _dQ tm, rfl =>
    ⟨Fintype.card Q - 1, tm.relabelState (FinTM.stateEquivFin ⟨1, Q, tm⟩)⟩

/-- **The code normal form is equivalent**. For a one-work-tape binary machine `M`, its code normal
form halts on `x` with output `w` within `t` steps if and only if `M` does. [AB09, §1.4]

**Proof sketch.** The relabelled machine's run is the image of `M`'s run under the state
bijection (`Turing.MultiTapeTM.relabelState_runFrom_init`); halting and output are preserved. -/
theorem FinTM.toCodeTM_computesInTime_iff (M : FinTM Bool) (hk : M.k = 1)
    (x output : List Bool) (t : ℕ) :
    (M.toCodeTM hk).toFinTM.ComputesInTime x output t ↔ M.ComputesInTime x output t := by
  rcases M with @⟨k, Q, hQ, dQ, tm⟩
  dsimp only at hk
  subst k
  exact FinTM.computesInTime_relabelState ⟨1, Q, tm⟩ _ x output t

/-- Every one-work-tape binary machine is equivalent, input by input and step for
step, to a coded machine.

**Proof sketch.** `State` carries `Fintype`/`DecidableEq` instances and is inhabited
by `q₀`, so `Fintype.equivFin` gives `e : State ≃ Fin n` with `n = numStates + 1` for
some `numStates`. Transport the transition function along `e` (renaming states with
`Turing.Action.mapState` and reading them back through `e.symm`); the induced map on
configurations is a bijection commuting with `step` (the tapes and heads are
untouched), so runs, halting, and outputs correspond at every step. The tape-count
cast uses `hk : M.k = 1`.

The implementation is the time clause of `Turing.exists_codeTM_spaceUsed`, whose witness
is this relabelling (`Turing.MultiTapeTM.relabelState`, from the shared state-renaming module
`TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.StateRenaming`), so that the relabelling is built once. -/
theorem exists_codeTM (M : FinTM Bool) (hk : M.k = 1) :
    ∃ M' : CodeTM, ∀ (x output : List Bool) (t : ℕ),
      M'.toFinTM.ComputesInTime x output t ↔ M.ComputesInTime x output t := by
  obtain ⟨M', h, -⟩ := exists_codeTM_spaceUsed M hk
  exact ⟨M', h⟩

end Turing
```

```
/-

Authors: Seyoon Ragavan
-/
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.CfgRecord
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.Seam
import TCSlib.Complexity.TuringMachine.Build.InputLength
import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Bitwise

set_option maxHeartbeats 0
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option autoImplicit false

/-!
# Machine-construction library: record tables and the deferred record rows (§12.8b)

The table layer of the §12.8 rich-alphabet design and the record rows its
statement gate deferred (`machine-library-design.md` §12.8a §8 item 10, §9
decisions 2 and 5, §12.8b). A **table** is a header field followed by entries,
each entry a fixed number of fields, all in the blank-separated field layout of
`Turing.joinFields`, with two blank cells on each side. The breadth-first
simulation of `NSPACE` in exponential time keeps its visited set in one; the
rows here append to a table, find the first entry a finite-state fold accepts,
copy field lists between tapes, and return from a table's end to its start.
The record rows write the record template and the initial record from binary
radius digits, decide record validity against the template, and enumerate the
valid records, which Savitch's midpoint recursion consumes.

**Status (fill continuation 5): 16 of 20 targets proved.** The layout facts,
end-to-start adapter, field-list copy, record-template writer and initial-record
constructor are proved. The four paused existential rows retain their proof sketches.
Append also has a proved reverse copier and seek-and-copy prefix. The
already-landed `Turing.RecordValid.joinFields_length` is admission-free as well.

## Design

* **The table layout** (decision 2 of §12.8a §9). `Turing.tableFields h es`
  is the header `h` followed by the fields of the entries `es`, and
  `Turing.TableAt` places its layout at an origin with two blank cells before
  the header and two after the last field. The header is nonempty, so the
  field list is never empty, every seek precondition is uniform, and the
  empty table is a header alone. Entries are addressed by
  `Turing.tableOffset`, the cell their first field starts at.
* **The end-to-start adapter** (decision 2, round-1 notes 14 and 42) is a real
  machine, `Turing.tableRewindTM`: skip back over the last field, then seek
  the start. Its exact framed contract is the composition of the two Catalog
  rows by one seam.
* **Find takes fuel.** The number of entries is not on any tape, and the one
  rich loop host, `Turing.counterLoopTMVia`, runs a counter, so
  `Turing.exists_tableFindTM` takes a digit word whose value exceeds the
  number of entries and restores it. The breadth-first host keeps one such word.
* **Field-list copy** `Turing.exists_fieldsCopyTM` moves a fixed number of
  fields between tapes; append and the enumeration are built on it, and the
  hosts use it for workspaces, table entries and Savitch's frames.
* **Record rows are existential modules** in the house style: a machine,
  entry and verdict anchors with `yes ≠ no`, a first-return time bound, an
  exact finish configuration that restores every head, the input position and
  the scratch, and a work-space clause bounding every work head through the
  verdict to `C·(size + 1)` cells of its entry position (round-1 major 1).
  Tape layouts are fixed and local, hosted by R1 (decision 4).
* **The template** `Turing.recordTemplate n s` carries what a record row cannot
  read off a candidate: the bound `n + 1` at the position width, and the
  `2s + 1`-cell window of a blank tape with its head at `0`.
* **The enumeration order is existential.** `Turing.exists_recordNextTM`
  exports a duplicate-free list of exactly the valid records and a module that
  walks it; the order the fill realizes is the odometer order, but no consumer
  reads it.

## Main definitions

* `Turing.recordLength` — the layout length of every record at `(k, n, s)`.
* `Turing.recordTemplate` — the widths template of the validity and
  enumeration rows.
* `Turing.tableFields`, `Turing.tableOffset`, `Turing.TableWF`,
  `Turing.TableAt` — the table layout, entry offsets, well-formedness, and
  placement on a tape.
* `Turing.tableRewindTM` — the end-to-start adapter.

## Main results

* `Turing.joinFields_length`, `Turing.fieldOffset_length`,
  `Turing.joinFields_cfgRecord_length`, `Turing.cfgRecord_field_ne_nil`,
  `Turing.cfgRecord_init`, `Turing.RecordValid.joinFields_length`,
  `Turing.recordValid_iff_exists_cfg`,
  `Turing.joinFields_recordTemplate_length`, `Turing.binDigits_posWidth_succ`
  — layout and record facts (proved).
* `Turing.TableWF.field_ne_nil`, `Turing.tableOffset_eq`,
  `Turing.tableOffset_length`, `Turing.TableAt.recordAt_take` — table facts
  (proved).
* `Turing.tableRewindTM_run_ofCfg` — the adapter's framed contract
  (proved).
* `Turing.exists_fieldsCopyTM` — field-list copy (proved).
* `Turing.exists_tableFindTM`, `Turing.exists_tableAppendTM` — the remaining
  table rows (statements).
* `Turing.exists_recordTemplateTM` — the record-template writer
  (proved; fill continuation 4).
* `Turing.exists_recordInitTM` — the initial-record constructor
  (proved; fill continuation 5).
* `Turing.exists_recordValidTM`, `Turing.exists_recordNextTM` — the remaining
  record rows of R8.7 (statements).
* `Turing.recordLength_eq` — the record length's formula, the specification API (user,
  2026-10-16).

## References

* [AB09] S. Arora, B. Barak, *Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach*,
  Cambridge University Press, 2009. (§4.1.1 and Claim 4.4: configurations
  described in `O(S(n))` bits; Theorem 4.2(iii), whose simulation searches the
  configuration graph keeping a table of visited configurations; Theorem 4.14
  (Savitch), whose recursion enumerates candidate midpoint configurations.)
-/

namespace Turing

/-! ### Layout lengths -/

/-- **The length of a field layout** (design §12.8b). A nonempty field list
lays out as its cells plus one separator between consecutive fields.

**Proof sketch.** Induct on the list: `List.intercalate` of a singleton is its
field, and each further field adds its length and one separator.

**Fill appendix.** Reuse the public layout induction in
`Turing.length_joinFields_add_one`; the remaining induction distributes the
sum of field lengths plus one. No second layout induction is introduced. -/
theorem joinFields_length {Γ : Type*} (fs : List (List Γ)) (hfs : fs ≠ []) :
    (joinFields fs).length = (fs.map List.length).sum + fs.length - 1 := by
  have h := length_joinFields_add_one fs hfs
  have hs : (fs.map (fun u => u.length + 1)).sum =
      (fs.map List.length).sum + fs.length := by
    clear h hfs
    induction fs with
    | nil => simp
    | cons u fs ih => simp only [List.map_cons, List.sum_cons, List.length_cons]; omega
  simp only [fieldOffset, List.take_length] at h
  omega

/-- **The end offset of a field layout** (design §12.8b; the formula of
`Turing.fieldOffset`'s docstring, made a lemma). For a nonempty field list,
`fieldOffset fs |fs|` is the layout length plus one: the cell after the blank
that ends the layout, where `Turing.seekEndTM` stops and a further field would
start.

**Proof sketch.** `fieldOffset fs |fs|` sums `|f| + 1` over all fields, which is
`Turing.joinFields_length` plus one. -/
theorem fieldOffset_length {Γ : Type*} (fs : List (List Γ)) (hfs : fs ≠ []) :
    fieldOffset fs fs.length = (joinFields fs).length + 1 := by
  exact (length_joinFields_add_one fs hfs).symm

/-- **The record length** (design §12.8b): the layout length of every record
with `k` tapes, input length `n` and radius `s` — `k` tape fields of `2s + 1`
cells, `posWidth n` position digits, the state and tag cells, and `k + 2`
separators. -/
def recordLength (k n s : ℕ) : ℕ := k * (2 * s + 1) + posWidth n + k + 4

/-- **The record length's formula** (the specification API, user 2026-10-16):
`recordLength k n s = k (2s + 1) + posWidth n + k + 4`, that is, `k` tape fields of `2s + 1`
cells, `posWidth n` position digits, the state and tag cells, and `k + 2` separators. -/
theorem recordLength_eq (k n s : ℕ) :
    recordLength k n s = k * (2 * s + 1) + posWidth n + k + 4 :=
  rfl

/-- **Every record has the record length** (design §12.8b). The layout of
`Turing.cfgRecord s c τ` has length `Turing.recordLength k |x| s`, whatever the
configuration and the tag. So the valid records at `(k, n, s)` all occupy the
same interval, and a row may rewrite one record into another in place.

**Proof sketch.** `Turing.joinFields_length` with the field lengths read off
`Turing.cfgRecord`: `1`, `posWidth |x|` (`binDigits` has its width), `2s + 1`
for each of the `k` tape fields, and `1`, over `k + 3` fields. -/
theorem joinFields_cfgRecord_length {k : ℕ} {Q T : Type} {x : List Bool} (s : ℕ)
    (c : Cfg k Bool Q x) (τ : T) :
    (joinFields (cfgRecord s c τ)).length = recordLength k x.length s := by
  rw [joinFields_length _ (by simp [cfgRecord]), cfgRecord_length]
  simp only [cfgRecord, Bind.bind, Pure.pure, ← List.map_eq_flatMap,
    binDigits, List.map_cons, List.map_append, List.map_map,
    Function.comp_def, List.length_map, List.length_range, List.map_const',
    List.length_finRange, List.sum_cons, List.sum_append, List.sum_replicate_nat,
    List.length_cons, List.length_nil, List.map_nil, List.sum_nil, recordLength]
  omega

/-- **Record fields are nonempty** (design §12.8b). No field of a record is
empty, so a table of records has no double blank inside it and the seek rows
apply.

**Proof sketch.** The state and tag fields have one cell, the tape fields
`2s + 1`, and the position field `posWidth |x| ≥ 1` cells, since
`Nat.bits (|x| + 1)` is nonempty. -/
theorem cfgRecord_field_ne_nil {k : ℕ} {Q T : Type} {x : List Bool} (s : ℕ)
    (c : Cfg k Bool Q x) (τ : T) : ∀ u ∈ cfgRecord s c τ, u ≠ [] := by
  have hwidth : 0 < posWidth x.length := by
    simpa only [posWidth, Nat.size_eq_bits_len] using
      (Nat.size_pos.mpr (Nat.succ_pos x.length))
  intro u hu
  simp only [cfgRecord, List.mem_cons, List.mem_append, List.mem_map,
    List.not_mem_nil, or_false] at hu
  rcases hu with rfl | rfl | ⟨i, hi, rfl⟩ | rfl
  · simp
  · intro h
    have := congrArg List.length h
    simp only [List.length_map, binDigits, List.length_range, List.length_nil] at this
    omega
  · intro h
    have := congrArg List.length h
    simp only [Bind.bind, Pure.pure, ← List.map_eq_flatMap,
      List.length_map, List.length_range, List.length_nil] at this
    omega
  · simp

/-- **The initial record** (design §12.8b). The record of the start
configuration `Cfg.init q₀ x` with tag `τ₀`: the state `some q₀`, the input
position `1` in `posWidth |x|` digits, `k` copies of the blank window with the
mark at its center (the head at cell `0`), and the tag. This is what
`Turing.exists_recordInitTM` writes.

**Proof sketch.** Unfold `Turing.cfgRecord` at `Cfg.init`: its work tapes are
blank, its heads at `0`, which is window index `s`, and its input position
is `1`. -/
theorem cfgRecord_init {k : ℕ} {Q T : Type} (x : List Bool) (s : ℕ) (q₀ : Q) (τ₀ : T) :
    cfgRecord s (Cfg.init q₀ x : Cfg k Bool Q x) τ₀ =
      [RecSym.st (some q₀)] :: ((binDigits (posWidth x.length) 1).map RecSym.digit) ::
        (List.replicate k ((List.range (2 * s + 1)).map fun j =>
            RecSym.cell none (decide (j = s))) ++
          [[RecSym.tag τ₀]]) := by
  have hmark (j : ℕ) : (0 : ℤ) = (j : ℤ) - s ↔ j = s := by omega
  simp only [cfgRecord, Cfg.init, Bind.bind, Pure.pure,
    ← List.map_eq_flatMap, List.map_map, Function.comp_def, hmark, List.map_const',
    List.length_finRange, Fin.val_one]

/-- **Valid records have the record length** (design §12.8b).

**Proof sketch.** A valid record is `Turing.cfgRecord s c τ` for a
configuration on an input of length `n`; apply
`Turing.joinFields_cfgRecord_length`. -/
theorem RecordValid.joinFields_length {k n s : ℕ} {Q T : Type}
    {fs : List (List (RecSym Q T))} (h : RecordValid k n s Q T fs) :
    (joinFields fs).length = recordLength k n s := by
  obtain ⟨x, c, τ, hx, -, rfl⟩ := h
  rw [joinFields_cfgRecord_length, hx]

/-- **Validity over a given input** (design §12.8b). A field list is a valid
record at input length `|x|` exactly when it is the record of a windowed
configuration on `x` itself. A record depends on its input only through the
input's length, so the windowed configurations of the actual input enumerate
every valid record; Savitch's midpoint enumeration rests on this.

**Proof sketch.** Backward: take the input `x`. Forward: a configuration on an
input `x'` with `|x'| = |x|` transports to `x` with the same state, work tapes,
heads and output and the input position cast along `|x'| = |x|`; its record and
window predicate are unchanged, since neither reads the input's symbols. -/
theorem recordValid_iff_exists_cfg {k : ℕ} {Q T : Type} (s : ℕ) (x : List Bool)
    (fs : List (List (RecSym Q T))) :
    RecordValid k x.length s Q T fs ↔
      ∃ (c : Cfg k Bool Q x) (τ : T), c.InWindow s ∧ cfgRecord s c τ = fs := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨y, c, τ, hy, hc, rfl⟩
    let d : Cfg k Bool Q x :=
      { state := c.state
        inputPos := ⟨c.inputPos.val, by simpa only [hy] using c.inputPos.isLt⟩
        workTapes := c.workTapes
        workTapePos := c.workTapePos
        output := c.output }
    refine ⟨d, τ, hc, ?_⟩
    simp only [cfgRecord, d, hy]
  · rintro ⟨c, τ, hc, hrec⟩
    exact ⟨x, c, τ, rfl, hc, hrec⟩

/-! ### The record template -/

/-- **The record template** (design §12.8b). Two fields over the record
alphabet: the bound `n + 1` in `posWidth n` digits, which also gives the
position width, and the window of a blank tape with its head at cell `0`:
`2s + 1` blank cells with the mark at the center. The validity and enumeration
rows read the widths and the position bound off it; its window field is the
tape field of the initial record (`Turing.cfgRecord_init`). -/
def recordTemplate (Q T : Type) (n s : ℕ) : List (List (RecSym Q T)) :=
  [(binDigits (posWidth n) (n + 1)).map RecSym.digit,
    (List.range (2 * s + 1)).map fun j => RecSym.cell none (decide (j = s))]

/-- **The template's length** (design §12.8b).

**Proof sketch.** Two fields of lengths `posWidth n` and `2s + 1`, and one
separator. -/
theorem joinFields_recordTemplate_length (Q T : Type) (n s : ℕ) :
    (joinFields (recordTemplate Q T n s)).length = posWidth n + 2 * s + 2 := by
  rw [joinFields_length _ (by simp [recordTemplate])]
  simp [recordTemplate, binDigits]
  omega

/-- **The template's bound field is `Nat.bits (n + 1)`** (design §12.8b). The
position width is the bit length of `n + 1`, so the fixed-width digits of
`n + 1` are its canonical binary word. A machine obtains the bound field from
`Turing.exists_inputLengthTM`'s `Nat.bits n` by one more increment.

**Proof sketch.** `binDigits w v` lists `v.testBit j` for `j < w`, and
`Nat.bits v` lists the same bits up to the bit length of `v`, which is
`posWidth n` at `v = n + 1`. -/
theorem binDigits_posWidth_succ (n : ℕ) :
    binDigits (posWidth n) (n + 1) = Nat.bits (n + 1) := by
  apply List.ext_getElem
  · simp [binDigits, posWidth]
  · intro j hj₁ hj₂
    simp only [binDigits, List.getElem_map, List.getElem_range]
    exact (Nat.testBit_eq_inth (n + 1) j).trans (List.getI_eq_getElem _ hj₂)

/-! ### Tables -/

/-- **The fields of a table** (design §12.8b, decision 2): the header `h`
followed by the fields of the entries `es` in order. -/
def tableFields {Γ : Type*} (h : List Γ) (es : List (List (List Γ))) : List (List Γ) :=
  h :: es.flatten

/-- **Entry offsets** (design §12.8b): the cell, relative to the table's origin,
at which entry `j` of the table starts. At `j = |es|` it is where a further
entry would start, two cells after the last field
(`Turing.tableOffset_length`). -/
def tableOffset {Γ : Type*} (h : List Γ) (es : List (List (List Γ))) (j : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  fieldOffset (tableFields h es) (1 + ((es.take j).map List.length).sum)

/-- **Well-formed tables** (design §12.8b): a nonempty header, and entries of
`m` fields each, every field nonempty. Under it two consecutive blanks occur
only at the table's ends, so the seek rows apply, and entries are found by
counting fields. -/
def TableWF {Γ : Type*} (m : ℕ) (h : List Γ) (es : List (List (List Γ))) : Prop :=
  h ≠ [] ∧ ∀ e ∈ es, e.length = m ∧ ∀ u ∈ e, u ≠ []

/-- **A table on a tape** (design §12.8b, decision 2): tape `r` holds the field
layout of the table with header `h` and entries `es` from the origin `o`, with
two blank cells before the header and two after the last field. The cells
beyond the sentinels are arbitrary; the head may be anywhere. -/
def TableAt {K : ℕ} {Γ S : Type*} {x : List Γ} (d : Cfg K Γ S x) (r : Fin K) (o : ℤ)
    (h : List Γ) (es : List (List (List Γ))) : Prop :=
  ∀ p : ℤ, -2 ≤ p → p ≤ ((joinFields (tableFields h es)).length : ℤ) + 1 →
    d.workTapes r (o + p) = fieldsTape (tableFields h es) p

/-- **Table fields are nonempty** (design §12.8b): the precondition of the seek
rows, from well-formedness.
